records.change: "became a living soul" becomes "started breathing"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew nephesh chayyah; the CEV reduces man's becoming a living soul to the start of breathing, losing a phrase often cited on human nature (1 Corinthians 15:45).

records.change: "your eyes shall be opened" becomes "see what you have done"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the serpent's promise of opened eyes is recast as seeing one's own deed, and "as gods" is read as "as God does", a common rendering of elohim.

records.change: Adds Cain's words "Let's go for a walk"
records.note: The Masoretic text has no words after "Cain said"; the CEV supplies them from the Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint and Syriac ("Let us go into the field").

records.change: "My spirit shall not always strive" becomes "life-giving breath remain"
records.note: The Hebrew verb is uncertain; the CEV follows the sense of the Septuagint ("remain") and reads it as a limit on lifespan. The KJV's reading, of God's Spirit striving with man, is lost.

records.change: "Sons of God" becomes "supernatural beings"
records.note: Translation choice: the Masoretic text has "sons of God", read by some as angels and by others as the line of Seth. The CEV settles on the first where the KJV leaves it open.

records.change: "Noah found grace" becomes "the LORD was pleased with Noah"
records.note: Translation choice: chen, favour or grace, is God's gift; the CEV makes it God's pleasure in Noah, which can read as earned.

records.change: "it shall be seen" becomes "it will be provided"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew yera'eh ("it will be seen" or "he will appear"); the CEV reads it as provision to match the place name.

records.change: "The virgin" becomes "a young woman"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew 'almah, also used in Isaiah 7:14, means a young woman of marriageable age; verse 16 still calls Rebekah a virgin.

records.change: "In thy seed shall all nations be blessed" becomes "They"
records.note: Translation choice: the singular "seed", which Galatians 3:16 applies to Christ, becomes plural descendants who are a blessing.

records.change: "Coat of many colours" becomes "fancy coat"
records.note: The Hebrew ketonet passim is uncertain; the KJV follows the Septuagint's "many-coloured", the CEV a general sense.

records.change: Drops Joseph's claim that he can "certainly divine"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew speaks of divination, as the KJV has; the CEV makes it "find out". The cup's use for divining is still mentioned in 44:5.

records.change: "digged down a wall" becomes "crippled cattle"; "a man" becomes "people"
records.note: The Masoretic vowels read shor (ox), which modern versions follow; the KJV read shur (wall). The CEV also drops the address to "my soul" and "mine honour".

records.change: Drops sceptre, lawgiver and "Shiloh"; messianic ruler made generic
records.note: A translation choice on a disputed Hebrew phrase: the KJV keeps "Shiloh" as a coming one to whom the peoples gather, long read as messianic; the CEV makes it Judah's own rule until nations bring tribute.

records.change: "Know that I am the LORD your God" loses the divine name
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew has the recognition formula with the name YHWH. The CEV keeps "I will be your God" and the name in 6:2.

records.change: Omits "I have made thee a god to Pharaoh"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew says Moses is made "elohim" to Pharaoh. The CEV keeps only Aaron as spokesman, as in 4:16.

records.change: Passover "ordinance for ever" becomes a yearly festival
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew "olam" makes it a perpetual statute. The CEV's "each year" says how often, not that it is permanent.

records.change: Unleavened bread "ordinance for ever" becomes "each year"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew calls it a perpetual statute for all generations. The CEV keeps the yearly keeping but not its permanence.

records.change: The angel, not the LORD, passes over the door
records.note: Translation choice; in the Hebrew the LORD passes over and keeps the destroyer out. The CEV makes the destroying angel the one who passes over.

records.change: "Ordinance ... for ever" becomes "each year"
records.note: Translation choice, as in 12:14 and 12:17; the Hebrew makes the Passover a perpetual ordinance. The CEV joins this verse with 12:25.

records.change: Israel obeys Moses and Aaron, not "as the LORD had commanded"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew says they did what the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron. The CEV drops the LORD as the source of the command.

records.change: Moses reports the LORD's words to the people, not the reverse
records.note: The Hebrew says Moses told the people's words to the LORD. The CEV reverses the direction of the report.

records.change: "A jealous God" becomes "I demand all your love"
records.note: Translation choice for the Hebrew "El qanna", a title of God used again in 34:14. The idea of exclusive devotion is kept, the title is not.

records.change: "kill" becomes "murder"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew ratsach is generally used of unlawful killing, which most modern versions express as "murder"; the KJV's "kill" is broader.

records.change: The servant is brought to the place of worship, not the judges
records.note: The Hebrew "ha-elohim" can mean God or judges; the KJV reads judges, the CEV reads God's sanctuary. A translation choice either way.

records.change: "her fruit depart" becomes "miscarriage"; harm limited to the woman
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "her children come out" can mean premature birth or miscarriage; the CEV's reading makes the fine cover a lost child and the harm clause the mother only, which bears on the status of the unborn.

records.change: Omits Aaron bearing Israel's judgment before the LORD continually
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew has the clause, and the names Urim and Thummim, which the CEV reduces to "two small objects".

records.change: "Make an atonement" on the altar becomes "purify the altar"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew kipper, which can mean purify or atone; the blood of the sin offering is kept. The atonement vocabulary of the Day of Atonement rite is lost here but kept in Leviticus 16.

records.change: "A ransom for his soul" becomes pay "to keep him safe"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Hebrew kopher (ransom); the idea of a ransom paid for each life is softened to a payment for protection from danger.

records.change: Joined verses 13-15 omit "to make an atonement for your souls"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the phrase; the CEV's merged verses 13-15 drop the purpose of the half shekel. The atonement money is presented only as a required payment.

records.change: "Atonement money" and "atonement for your souls" omitted
records.note: A translation choice, not a textual one: the Hebrew twice names atonement here. The CEV reduces it to upkeep money and a memorial, losing the link between the payment and atonement.

records.change: Omits God swearing "by thine own self" and inheriting "for ever"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; God's oath by himself (cited in Hebrews 6:13) and the permanence of the land grant are both dropped.

records.change: Omits "whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the divine name "Jealous" is reduced to "I demand your complete loyalty". The same attribute is stated in Exodus 20:5.

records.change: "The blood of my sacrifice" becomes "sacrifice an animal"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew names the blood of the sacrifice, which the CEV drops. The parallel in Exodus 23:18 carries the same law.

records.change: Touching makes one holy becomes must be made holy before touching
records.note: A translation choice on an ambiguous Hebrew clause ("whatever touches them shall be holy"). The KJV reads holiness as passed on by contact, as the CEV itself does at 6:27; here the CEV makes it a prerequisite.

records.change: "The scapegoat" becomes a goat sent "to the demon Azazel"
records.note: A translation choice on the Hebrew la'aza'zel: the KJV reads it as the goat that goes away, the CEV as a name and adds "demon", which the text does not say. The goat still bears away the people's sins in 16:10 and 16:21-22.

records.change: Adds "This law will never change" to the Sabbath verse
records.note: The Masoretic text of this verse has no "statute for ever" clause; the CEV adds it as a translation choice. The perpetual-statute wording belongs to other feast verses (e.g. Leviticus 23:14, 21).

records.change: "Everlasting covenant" becomes "Israel's agreement with me"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew berit olam is "everlasting covenant". The CEV keeps continuity with "in all generations" but drops the covenant's everlasting character.

records.change: Devoted things "must be completely destroyed", not merely unredeemable
records.note: The Masoretic text says devoted things cannot be sold or redeemed and are most holy to the LORD (they go to the priests, Numbers 18:14). Destruction applies to devoted persons in 27:29; the CEV extends it here as a translation choice.

records.change: Omits that Nadab was "the firstborn"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew names Nadab as the firstborn (bekor). The CEV lists the four sons without it.

records.change: Makes Hobab, not Raguel, Moses' father-in-law
records.note: The Hebrew is ambiguous as to whether "Moses' father in law" refers to Raguel or Hobab (Judges 4:11 calls Hobab hoten). The KJV applies it to Raguel; the CEV to Hobab and drops Raguel.

records.change: "The spirit which is upon thee" becomes "your authority"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew is ruach, the spirit on Moses, which the CEV renders as authority, losing the reference to God's Spirit shared with the elders.

records.change: Spirit called "authority"; prophesied "only this one time"
records.note: Ruach is again rendered "authority", though the CEV keeps "the LORD's Spirit" later in the verse. "Did not cease" versus "did not do so again" is an ambiguity in the Hebrew (lo yasafu); modern versions mostly read the latter.

records.change: Omits "forgiving iniquity and transgression"
records.note: The Masoretic text includes God forgiving iniquity in this quotation of Exodus 34:6-7; the CEV's wording here leaves it out. God's forgiveness is still asked for in 14:19.

records.change: Omits "all the earth shall be filled with the glory"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the CEV replaces it with "my power has no limit". The same promise is stated in Habakkuk 2:14 and Isaiah 11:9.

records.change: Priest's "atonement" becomes the priest praying for forgiveness
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew kipper refers to the priest making atonement through the offering. The CEV recasts it as prayer, though it keeps the sacrifices.

records.change: "Make an atonement" becomes "ask me to forgive you"
records.note: As in 15:25, kipper (make atonement) is rendered as the priest asking forgiveness, which changes the priest's role from sacrificial to intercessory.

records.change: "God of the spirits of all flesh" becomes "you gave life"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew has the divine title, which the CEV paraphrases as a statement. The same title recurs in Numbers 27:16.

records.change: "He also shall perish for ever" made "Cyprus itself will be ruined"
records.note: The Masoretic "he" is ambiguous (the invader or Eber) and "for ever" is dropped; the CEV names Chittim as the one ruined, a translation choice that narrows the prophecy's referent.

records.change: "Hang them up before the LORD" becomes killing guilty leaders; adds "Maybe"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew says to take all the heads and expose them before the LORD; the CEV limits it to those responsible and makes the turning of God's anger uncertain ("Maybe then") where the KJV states its purpose.

records.change: Omits "a man in whom is the spirit"
records.note: The Masoretic text describes Joshua as a man with the spirit (ruach); the CEV replaces this with "can do the job", losing the ground of his appointment. Deuteronomy 34:9 still says he was full of the spirit of wisdom.

records.change: Omits "to make an atonement for our souls"
records.note: The Hebrew states the gold was brought to make atonement before the LORD; the CEV makes it a thank-offering "for watching over us", a translation choice that drops the atonement.

records.change: Omits "be guiltless before the LORD, and before Israel"
records.note: The CEV renders the clause as no longer having to stay with the others, losing the statement that fulfilling the vow leaves them guiltless before God.

records.change: "O Lord GOD" becomes "Our LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew is Adonai YHWH; the CEV compresses the double title into one, a translation choice.

records.change: Says the LORD put the stars there "for other nations to worship"
records.note: The Hebrew says the LORD "allotted" the heavenly bodies to all peoples; the CEV reads this as God appointing them as objects of worship, an interpretive rendering the KJV does not make.

records.change: "Is a consuming fire, a jealous God" softened to "can be like a fire"
records.note: The Hebrew states what God is; the CEV turns it into a conditional simile tied to idolatry, a translation choice. Hebrews 12:29 quotes the verse as a direct statement.

records.change: "The LORD our God is one LORD" becomes "the only true God"
records.note: The Shema's "one" (echad) can be read as oneness or as "the LORD alone"; the CEV chooses exclusivity and drops the statement of God's oneness, which Mark 12:29 quotes.

records.change: Omits "it shall be our righteousness"
records.note: The CEV joins verses 24-25 and renders the result as protection and success, dropping the Hebrew's statement that obedience "shall be our righteousness".

records.change: Moses bows "in front of the sacred tent", not "before the LORD"
records.note: A translation choice with no basis in the Hebrew, which says only "before the LORD"; the tent is not in the text here.

records.change: "The LORD is his inheritance" becomes a promise to provide
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew says the LORD himself is Levi's inheritance, which the CEV turns into material provision.

records.change: "Fear the LORD" softened to "respect"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew yare' is the usual word for fearing God. The CEV keeps "fear and trembling" in 13:4.

records.change: "God of gods, and Lord of lords" becomes "more powerful than" them
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew titles are paraphrased as a comparison, losing the divine titles quoted in 1 Timothy 6:15 and Revelation 17:14.

records.change: Omits "the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben"
records.note: A paraphrase that drops the genealogy in the Hebrew; the event itself is kept.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from the promise to descendants
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew 'ad 'olam is left out, so the blessing loses its perpetuity.

records.change: Omits "an holy people"
records.note: A paraphrase that drops the Hebrew qadosh; being chosen and belonging to the LORD are kept.

records.change: "Fear the LORD thy God always" becomes "respect"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew yare', the usual word for fearing God.

records.change: Omits "the LORD thy God shall bless thee in all"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the CEV leaves it out here, though the same promise stands in 15:10.

records.change: "The LORD is their inheritance" becomes provision
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew says the LORD himself is the Levites' inheritance, as in 10:9.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from the priests' appointment
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew kol-hayyamim (all the days) is rendered only as "and their descendants".

records.change: "Be perfect with the LORD" becomes a ban on disgusting things
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew tamim (blameless) before God is turned into a prohibition, and the LORD is not named.

records.change: "Lay hold on her" becomes "talks her into"; "virgin" dropped
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew tapas means to seize, so the CEV changes force into seduction, and betulah is left out.

records.change: Narrowed to "no peace treaty"; omits prosperity and "for ever"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Hebrew, which forbids seeking their peace or good all your days.

records.change: "whore" and "sodomite" become "temple prostitutes"
records.note: A translation choice for qedeshah and qadesh ("consecrated ones"); the CEV reads cult prostitution and drops the KJV's male and female distinction.

records.change: "An holy people" becomes "his own special people"
records.note: A paraphrase that drops the Hebrew 'am qadosh (holy people), as in 14:2.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from the curses on descendants
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew 'ad 'olam is left out, so the sign loses its lasting force.

records.change: Omits trembling heart, failing eyes, sorrow; adds longing for home
records.note: The CEV replaces the Masoretic text's list with a paraphrase of its own; restlessness is kept.

records.change: "Secret things belong unto the LORD" becomes unexplained present and future
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew contrasts hidden things that belong to God with revealed things given to Israel, which the CEV rewords.

records.change: "Circumcise thine heart" becomes "make you willing to obey"
records.note: A translation choice that drops the Hebrew image taken up in Romans 2:29 and Colossians 2:11; God changing the heart is kept.

records.change: "Number of the children of Israel" becomes a guardian angel per nation
records.note: The CEV follows the Septuagint ("angels of God") and a Dead Sea Scroll (4QDeut-j, "sons of God") instead of the Masoretic "sons of Israel".

records.change: "Rock of his salvation" becomes "only place of safety"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew yeshu'ah, which the KJV renders "salvation"; God as Rock is kept.

records.change: "The lowest hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew she'ol, which modern translations usually render as the grave or the place of the dead.

records.change: Adds heavens rejoicing and "all gods to bow down"
records.note: The CEV follows the Septuagint and a Dead Sea Scroll (4QDeut-q) instead of the Masoretic text; Hebrews 1:6 quotes the Septuagint's longer reading.

records.change: "ten thousands of saints" become "warriors"; "fiery law" becomes "fire"
records.note: A translation choice on difficult Hebrew (esh dat, "fire of law"); the CEV drops the giving of the law and turns the holy ones into an army.

records.change: "By him" becomes "The LORD Most High"
records.note: The CEV follows an emendation of the Hebrew 'alayw (upon him) to 'Elyon (Most High), not the Masoretic text.

records.change: "did worship" becomes "bowed down to the ground"
records.note: The Hebrew verb can mean either bowing or worship; a translation choice. The KJV's "worship" is often read as the commander accepting worship, a sign of a divine figure; verse 15's holy ground remains.

records.change: Says all the builder's children will die
records.note: The Masoretic text names only the firstborn and the youngest son; the CEV's "all his children" goes beyond it. 1 Kings 16:34 records the fulfilment with the two sons.

records.change: Call to give glory and confess becomes a verdict of guilt
records.note: A paraphrase choice; the Hebrew is Joshua urging Achan to give glory to God and confess. The CEV turns the plea into a statement that God has found him guilty.

records.change: "LORD was their inheritance" becomes "would always provide for them"
records.note: A paraphrase choice; the Hebrew says the LORD himself is the Levites' inheritance, not only their provider. The same idea is kept in Numbers 18:20.

records.change: Othniel made Caleb's nephew rather than his brother
records.note: The Hebrew "Othniel son of Kenaz, brother of Caleb" is read by the KJV with Othniel as the brother; the CEV takes "brother" with Kenaz. A translation choice of the ambiguous phrase.

records.change: "before God" becomes "near the sacred tent"
records.note: A paraphrase choice; the Masoretic text says only that they presented themselves before God, and names no tent at Shechem. The tabernacle stood at Shiloh (Joshua 18:1).

records.change: Drops "holy God" and "jealous God"; softens "will not forgive"
records.note: A paraphrase; the Hebrew names God as holy and jealous and says he will not forgive transgressions. The CEV gives "fearsome" and "one true God" instead, losing both attributes.

records.change: Othniel made Caleb's nephew rather than his younger brother
records.note: The Hebrew "Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother" is read by the KJV with Othniel as the brother; the CEV takes it as Kenaz. A translation choice; see also Joshua 15:17.

records.change: Omits God as the one who subdued Jabin
records.note: The Masoretic text makes God the subject; the CEV says the Israelites defeated Jabin. God's part in the victory is still stated in verses 14-15.

records.change: Omits Sinai and the mountains melting "before the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text links the quaking mountains to the LORD's presence and to Sinai; the CEV's verse leaves both out. A paraphrase choice, not a textual difference.

records.change: "found grace in thy sight" becomes "talking to the LORD"
records.note: A paraphrase choice; the Hebrew asks for a sign as a favour and does not name the speaker. The CEV identifies Gideon's visitor as the LORD, as verse 14 does.

records.change: Omits "O Lord GOD" and "face to face"
records.note: A paraphrase choice; the Hebrew has Gideon cry to the Lord GOD because he saw the angel face to face. The CEV keeps only his fear of dying.

records.change: "honour God and man" becomes "people and gods"
records.note: The Hebrew elohim can mean God or gods; the CEV takes the plural, fitting the fable. The KJV reads it as God, honoured by the oil of offerings.

records.change: "cheereth God and man" becomes "people and gods"
records.note: The Hebrew elohim can mean God or gods; the CEV takes the plural. The KJV reads it as God, whose drink offerings were of wine.

records.change: Omits God sending "an evil spirit"
records.note: The Masoretic text says God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; the CEV says only that God turned the leaders against him. The spirit sent by God also appears in 1 Samuel 16:14.

records.change: Omits "shall be the LORD's" and "burnt offering"
records.note: The Masoretic text vows that whatever comes out shall be the LORD's and offered as a burnt offering; the CEV says "whoever" will be sacrificed. The wording bears on how Jephthah's vow is read.

records.change: Name "secret" becomes "you couldn't understand it"
records.note: The Hebrew pil'i means "wonderful", the word of Isaiah 9:6, often read as a sign of a divine visitor. The CEV keeps the sense of mystery but loses the word.

records.change: "we have seen God" becomes "We have seen an angel"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "God" (elohim); the CEV substitutes "an angel". This loses Manoah's identification of the angel of the LORD with God, also seen in Genesis 32:30.

records.change: Jonathan's grandfather named Moses, not Manasseh
records.note: The Masoretic text has Manasseh with a raised nun, widely taken as a scribal change from Moses; some Septuagint copies and the Vulgate read Moses. The CEV follows that reading.

records.change: Drops that the LORD gives the offspring
records.note: Translation choice; the Masoretic text says the seed is what "the LORD shall give". The CEV keeps the blessing but not God as its source.

records.change: Omits "there is none holy as the LORD"
records.note: Translation choice; the Masoretic text opens with God's holiness, which the CEV folds into "no other god is like you". His uniqueness is kept, his holiness is not named.

records.change: "His anointed" becomes "your chosen king"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew is mashiach, which the KJV renders "anointed" and many read as pointing to the Messiah. The CEV makes it a generic king.

records.change: "Lightly esteemed" becomes "put a curse on"; despise becomes hate
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew says those who despise God will be lightly regarded. The CEV makes it a stronger, active curse.

records.change: "Mine anointed" becomes "my chosen king"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew mashiach ("anointed") is given a generic rendering, losing the verbal link to the Messiah some readers see here.

records.change: Adds that they cried "to their gods"
records.note: The Masoretic text says only that the city's cry went up to heaven. The CEV adds prayer to pagan gods, which the Hebrew does not state.

records.change: Seventy men die, not fifty thousand and seventy
records.note: The Masoretic text reads 50,070; a few Hebrew manuscripts and Josephus have 70, which the CEV follows. The KJV follows the Masoretic number.

records.change: "reigned one year" becomes "was a young man"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "a son of a year", evidently defective; the KJV reads a length of reign and the CEV guesses Saul's youth.

records.change: Omits "a man after his own heart"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew describes David as a man after God's heart, a phrase quoted in Acts 13:22. The CEV says only that God has chosen the next leader.

records.change: "Bring the ark of God" becomes asking God
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "ark of God"; the Septuagint reads "ephod". The CEV follows the Septuagint's sense of seeking an oracle.

records.change: Evil spirit "from God" becomes "the LORD let"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew says the evil spirit was from God. The CEV softens this to God permitting it, though 16:16 keeps "from God".

records.change: Statement "evil not found in thee" becomes a prayer
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew states that no evil has been found in David. The CEV turns it into a wish that he will do no evil.

records.change: Omits "bound in the bundle of life with the LORD"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew image of the soul bound up with God, which some read of life beyond death, becomes simply "keep you safe".

records.change: Adds "down here in the world of the dead"
records.note: The Hebrew says only "thou and thy sons shall be with me". The CEV makes explicit a place of the dead that the verse implies but does not name.

records.change: Drops "for ever"; says no one will take his kingdom away
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "for ever" ('ad 'olam); the CEV's rendering is a translation choice. The everlasting throne is central to the messianic reading of the Davidic covenant (Luke 1:32-33), though "always" is kept in 7:16.

records.change: "Is this the manner of man" becomes "the way you usually treat people"
records.note: The Hebrew torat ha'adam is obscure; the CEV takes it as a question about God's dealings, a translation choice. Some interpreters read it as a charter for mankind with a messianic sense, which the rendering closes off.

records.change: Omits "establish it for ever" from David's prayer
records.note: The Masoretic text has "for ever"; the CEV's shortening is a translation choice. The permanence of the promise is still stated in 7:16 and 7:29.

records.change: "Syria" becomes "Edom"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads Aram (Syria); the CEV follows the Septuagint and the parallel 1 Chronicles 18:11, which read Edom. The two words differ by one similar Hebrew letter.

records.change: Drops "kindness of God"; David's own kindness only
records.note: The Hebrew reads "the kindness (hesed) of God"; the CEV's omission is a translation choice. It loses the sense of covenant kindness shown in God's name, echoing 1 Samuel 20:14.

records.change: "Thy master's son" becomes "Saul's family and servants"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "your master's son"; the CEV's "family" resembles Greek readings with "house" and smooths the tension with Mephibosheth eating at David's table. A translation choice with some textual support.

records.change: Captives put under saws becomes forced labour with tools
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "put them to" saws and axes can mean execution or labour; the CEV reads work and brick-making, removing the KJV's picture of torture.

records.change: Adds "in Hebron" to Absalom's vow
records.note: The Masoretic text lacks "in Hebron"; the CEV follows Greek (Lucianic) manuscripts that add it. The place is implied by 15:9.

records.change: Ithra "an Israelite" becomes "from the family of Ishmael"
records.note: The Masoretic text here reads Israelite; the CEV follows 1 Chronicles 2:17 and some Greek manuscripts, which read Ishmaelite.

records.change: Elhanan kills Goliath himself, not "the brother of Goliath"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "killed Goliath"; the KJV supplies "the brother of" in italics from 1 Chronicles 20:5, which names him Lahmi. The CEV follows the Hebrew as it stands, which seems to contradict 1 Samuel 17.

records.change: "Horn of my salvation" becomes "my powerful weapon"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew metaphor. The KJV wording is echoed of Christ in Luke 1:69; rescue is still stated at the verse's end.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol, the grave or realm of the dead, which the KJV often renders "hell"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment.

records.change: "Maketh my way perfect" becomes "you set me free"
records.note: The Hebrew verb is uncertain and the text differs from Psalm 18:32; the CEV's rendering is a translation choice that loses "perfect".

records.change: "Everlasting covenant" becomes a promise; opening clause made positive
records.note: The KJV reads the first clause as a negative, many modern versions as a question expecting "yes"; the CEV turns it into a statement. The covenant with David, read messianically, becomes "promise" and "all my salvation" becomes help.

records.change: "Chief among three" becomes "leader of the Thirty"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "three"; the CEV follows two Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac, which read "thirty", as in 23:19.

records.change: "A young virgin" becomes "a young woman"
records.note: The Hebrew na'arah betulah names her as a virgin; the CEV's rendering drops the word. Her virginity matters to the story (1:4 says David did not know her).

records.change: "Repent" and their confession of sin become "feel sorry"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the Hebrew speaks of turning back (shuv) and a threefold confession, which the CEV reduces to regret and a request for forgiveness. Turning from sin is kept in 8:35.

records.change: Omits that the LORD loved Israel "for ever"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew le'olam (for ever) is dropped, so the permanence of God's love for Israel is not stated here.

records.change: Omits "the cause was from the LORD"
records.note: A paraphrase in the CEV's joined verses 15-20; the Hebrew says the king's refusal was brought about by the LORD, which the CEV drops, keeping only that Ahijah's prophecy came true.

records.change: "sodomites" becomes "prostitutes at the shrines"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew qadesh, read by modern versions as shrine prostitution rather than sodomy.

records.change: "sodomites" becomes "prostitutes at the shrines"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew qedeshim, read by modern versions as shrine prostitution rather than sodomy.

records.change: "Hast turned their heart back" becomes "will turn"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew perfect says God has turned the people's hearts, which the CEV makes a future hope. Some take it as a prophetic perfect, so the sense is debated.

records.change: "What have I done to thee?" becomes "remember what I've done for you"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; Elijah's question leaving Elisha free is turned into a reminder of the call, which changes the tone of his reply.

records.change: "Ye shall know that I am the LORD" becomes "the LORD is in control"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; God's self-revelation formula, spoken in the first person, is reduced to a statement about his power.

records.change: "ashes upon his face" becomes "a bandage"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew aphar, which modern lexicons take as a headband or bandage rather than ashes.

records.change: Omits "The LORD forbid it me"
records.note: A paraphrase; Naboth's refusal rests on the LORD's law of family inheritance in the Hebrew, while the CEV gives only family tradition.

records.change: The "lying spirit" who volunteers is dropped
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the spirit that offers to deceive becomes the speaker's plan to make the prophets lie, so the spirit is no longer named.

records.change: "Put a lying spirit" becomes "made all your prophets lie"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the spirit in the heavenly council is dropped and the LORD made the direct cause of the lie.

records.change: Omits "the Spirit of the LORD"
records.note: A paraphrase; Zedekiah's taunt names the Spirit of the LORD as the source of prophecy, which the CEV reduces to the LORD speaking.

records.change: "Double portion of thy spirit" becomes more power than other prophets
records.note: An interpretive paraphrase; the CEV reads the firstborn's double share (Deuteronomy 21:17) as leadership of the prophets and turns "spirit" into "power".

records.change: "My father... the chariot of Israel" becomes chariots taking him
records.note: A translation choice; in the Hebrew Elisha hails Elijah as Israel's chariots and horsemen, a title repeated of Elisha in 13:14, whereas the CEV makes the chariots take Elijah away.

records.change: "The spirit of Elijah" becomes "Elijah's power"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew ruach; the spirit resting on Elisha is reduced to power, as in 2:9.

records.change: Omits that the LORD spoke and "hath done" what he said
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the Hebrew stresses the LORD's word and his act in fulfilling it, which the CEV reduces to Elijah's promise coming true.

records.change: "The testimony" becomes "instructions for ruling the nation"
records.note: An interpretive translation of the Hebrew 'edut, usually taken as the covenant law (compare Deuteronomy 17:18); the CEV makes it a manual for kingship.

records.change: Omits covenant "that they should be the LORD'S people"
records.note: A paraphrase; the Hebrew describes a covenant making Judah the LORD's people, which the CEV reduces to a promise of faithfulness.

records.change: "My father... the chariot of Israel" becomes a question about chariots
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew hails Elisha as Israel's chariots and horsemen, as Elisha said of Elijah in 2:12, and the CEV turns the title into a question.

records.change: "The LORD said not" becomes "the LORD had promised"
records.note: A paraphrase; the Hebrew says only that the LORD had not decreed Israel's destruction, which the CEV turns into an explicit promise.

records.change: Omits sprinkling "the blood of his peace offerings"
records.note: The Hebrew has the blood rite; the CEV paraphrases the offerings by their purpose and leaves it out. A translation choice; the blood is still named in 16:15.

records.change: "did not believe in the LORD" becomes "refused to worship"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew verb means to trust or believe, and the CEV renders it as worship, shifting the fault from unbelief to neglect of worship.

records.change: Adds Jeroboam standing at the altar at a festival
records.note: The added words are in the Septuagint but not the Masoretic text the KJV follows; the CEV takes them from the Greek. The event itself is told in 1 Kings 13:1-2.

records.change: Geshur and Aram capture the towns, not Jair
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew can be read with Geshur and Aram as subject, as most modern versions do; the KJV makes the Israelite the one who took them.

records.change: Hur is Caleb's son, not Caleb "the son of Hur"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "Caleb the son of Hur"; the CEV follows the Septuagint and a repointed reading ("sons of Hur"), which agrees with 2:19 and 4:4.

records.change: "Assir" read as "prisoner", not as a son's name
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew assir means "captive". The CEV makes Shealtiel Jehoiachin's son, as in Matthew 1:12; the KJV lists Assir as a son.

records.change: "the father of Etam" becomes Etam's own sons
records.note: The CEV follows the Septuagint ("sons of Etam") rather than the Masoretic "father of Etam", and adds that Etam was Hur's descendant.

records.change: Pul and Tiglath-pileser made one king; Pul dropped
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "and" is read as "that is", since Pul was Tiglath-pileser's Babylonian name; the KJV names them as two.

records.change: Samuel's firstborn is "Joel", not "Vashni"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "the firstborn Vashni"; the CEV follows the Septuagint's Lucianic text and Syriac, which name Joel as in 6:33 and 1 Samuel 8:2.

records.change: Names "the father of Gibeon" as Jeiel
records.note: The Masoretic text leaves him unnamed here; the CEV supplies the name from the parallel 9:35, as some Septuagint manuscripts do.

records.change: Adds "Ner" to the list of sons
records.note: Ner is not in the Masoretic text of this verse; the CEV adds him from the Septuagint and the parallel list in 9:36.

records.change: "Stablish his throne for ever" becomes "no one will take his kingdom"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew has 'ad 'olam, for ever. The eternal throne of David's son, read messianically, is kept elsewhere in the chapter (17:14, 17:27).

records.change: "He shall be my son" becomes "like a son to me"
records.note: The Hebrew says he will be to me for a son, which the CEV softens to a likeness; Hebrews 1:5 applies the parallel 2 Samuel 7:14 to Christ. The everlasting throne becomes "one of his descendants will always rule".

records.change: Omits "for ever" of Aaron's priesthood and burning incense
records.note: The Masoretic text twice says for ever ('ad 'olam) of Aaron's appointment; the CEV's paraphrase drops both, and incense becomes sacrifices in general.

records.change: "Chosen him to be my son" becomes "like a son to me"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew says God chose him to be his son. The CEV makes it a likeness and drops "chosen", as in 22:10.

records.change: Omits "by the spirit" as the source of David's plans
records.note: The Hebrew has beruach, which may mean in his mind or by the Spirit; the CEV leaves it out. That the plans came from God is still said in 28:19.

records.change: "Sat on the throne of the LORD" becomes "became king"
records.note: A translation choice; the Masoretic text calls David's throne the LORD's throne, a point in the messianic reading of the Davidic kingdom, which the CEV drops.

records.change: "Thine anointed" becomes "your chosen kings"
records.note: The Hebrew is meshicheka, your anointed one (singular), a term read messianically; the CEV makes it plural and general.

records.change: Omits "set thee on his throne, to be king for the LORD"
records.note: A translation choice; the Masoretic text says Solomon sits on God's own throne as king for the LORD, which the CEV reduces to "made you king of Israel".

records.change: Makes Abihail Mahalath's mother, not Rehoboam's second wife
records.note: The Hebrew can be read either way; the KJV takes Abihail as a second wife, the CEV (with most modern versions, since 11:19 has one wife bearing) as Mahalath's mother.

records.change: "The Spirit of God came upon" becomes "God spoke to"
records.note: A translation choice; the Masoretic text names the Spirit of God resting on Azariah, which the CEV leaves out. The CEV keeps the Spirit in 20:14 and 24:20.

records.change: Ahaziah's age "forty and two" becomes twenty-two
records.note: The Masoretic text reads 42; the CEV follows some Septuagint manuscripts, the Syriac and 2 Kings 8:26, which read 22.

records.change: "Azariah" becomes "Ahaziah"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads Azariah; the CEV follows some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint and 2 Kings 8:29 in reading Ahaziah, the name used in the rest of the chapter.

records.change: "Understanding in the visions of God" becomes "taught him to obey God"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "in the seeing of God"; the CEV follows some Hebrew manuscripts and the Septuagint, "in the fear of God". It also ties Uzziah's faithfulness to Zechariah's lifetime rather than to his seeking the LORD.

records.change: Jehoiachin's age "eight" becomes eighteen
records.note: Most Masoretic manuscripts read 8; the CEV follows some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint and 2 Kings 24:8, which read 18.

records.change: Omits that Zedekiah was Jehoiachin's "brother"
records.note: The Masoretic text says "his brother" (kinsman); 2 Kings 24:17 calls Zedekiah his uncle. The CEV drops the word, apparently to avoid the apparent conflict.

records.change: "The work of their Lord" becomes work "they were assigned"
records.note: The Hebrew plural "their lords" can mean God or human overseers; the KJV reads it as the Lord, the CEV as human supervisors. A translation choice.

records.change: Johanan "son of Eliashib" becomes "grandson"; records stop at his death
records.note: The Hebrew says "son", which can mean descendant; Nehemiah 12:10-11 makes Johanan (Jonathan) Eliashib's grandson, and the CEV harmonises. It also recasts the verse as records ending after him.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from the ban on Ammonites and Moabites
records.note: The Masoretic text has "for ever", as in Deuteronomy 23:3; the CEV leaves it out, losing the permanence of the exclusion.

records.change: "The sons of God" becomes "the angels"
records.note: The Hebrew is "sons of God"; the CEV gives the common interpretation, as the Septuagint does ("angels of God"). The same choice is made in Job 2:1.

records.change: "The sons of God" becomes "the angels"
records.note: As in Job 1:6: an interpretive rendering of the Hebrew "sons of God", in line with the Septuagint.

records.change: "A spirit passed before my face" becomes "a wind blew"
records.note: The Hebrew ruach means spirit or wind; the KJV reads a spirit being in Eliphaz's vision, the CEV a wind. A translation choice that changes what Eliphaz saw.

records.change: "I have sinned" becomes "if I sin"; burden to God
records.note: A translation choice: the confession is made conditional, "preserver of men" becomes a watcher, and "a burden to myself" follows the Septuagint and scribal tradition ("to you").

records.change: Job wouldn't believe God listened becomes God "would not hear"
records.note: The Masoretic text says Job would not believe God had listened; the CEV makes it God's refusal to hear his case. A translation choice that shifts the doubt from Job to God.

records.change: "Deeper than hell" becomes "deeper than the grave"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol, which the KJV renders variously as hell, grave or pit; the CEV chooses "grave". A translation choice, not a textual difference.

records.change: God giving abundantly becomes robbers boasting "God is in our hands"
records.note: A translation choice for ambiguous Hebrew (literally "who brings God in his hand"); the KJV has God prospering the wicked, the CEV has them claiming control of God.

records.change: Omits "there is a spirit in man"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; Elihu's claim that understanding comes through a spirit in man, the breath of the Almighty, is reduced to wisdom coming from God.

records.change: "Sons of God" becomes "angels"
records.note: An interpretive translation of the Hebrew bene elohim; the reading as angels is common, but the CEV removes the phrase that links this verse with Genesis 6:2 and Job 1:6.

records.change: "Repent" becomes sitting in ashes "to show my sorrow"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew nicham is often rendered repent, though some read "am comforted". The CEV keeps sorrow but not a turning.

records.change: "My Son... begotten thee" becomes "my son... become your father"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew yelidtikha is "I have begotten you". The CEV's lower-case son reads it of the king, though Acts 13:33 and Hebrews 1:5 apply it to Christ.

records.change: "Kiss the Son" becomes "respect his son"; wrath moved to the LORD
records.note: The Hebrew nashqu-bar is disputed (some emend it); the KJV reads the Son's wrath and trust in him, while the CEV moves both to the LORD, losing the messianic focus.

records.change: "The son of man" becomes "us weaklings"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew ben-adam means a human, but Hebrews 2:6-8 applies this verse to Christ, and the CEV's plural loses the singular.

records.change: "angels" becomes "you yourself"; "him" becomes "us"
records.note: A translation choice for elohim, where the KJV follows the Septuagint reading quoted in Hebrews 2:7; the CEV's plural "us" also loses the singular "him" that Hebrews 2:9 applies to Jesus.

records.change: "Turned into hell" becomes "go down to the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew Sheol; the KJV reads the fate of the wicked as hell, the CEV as the realm of the dead, so the note of punishment is softer.

records.change: "Thine Holy One" becomes "I am your chosen one"; hell becomes grave
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew chasid is "holy/godly one". Acts 2:27 and 13:35 apply the verse to Christ's resurrection, which the CEV's wording still allows but no longer marks.

records.change: Worldly men God fills become "those you love" whom God feeds
records.note: The Hebrew is difficult (some read tsephunekha as "your treasured ones"); the KJV describes the wicked prospering, the CEV turns the line into God's care for his own.

records.change: Voice heard everywhere becomes "never the sound of a voice"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew is "no speech, no words, their voice not heard"; the KJV's italic words make it heard in every language, the CEV makes the heavens silent.

records.change: "They pierced my hands and my feet" becomes "tearing at"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads ka'ari, "like a lion"; the Septuagint and a Dead Sea psalms scroll support "pierced/dug", which the KJV follows. The CEV's "tearing" loses the link with the crucifixion.

records.change: "Your heart shall live for ever" becomes "live in hope"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text, which says the heart will live for ever (la'ad); the CEV drops the permanence.

records.change: "O ye mighty" becomes "angels in heaven"
records.note: An interpretive translation of the Hebrew bene elim (sons of the mighty/of God); reading them as angels is common but is the CEV's choice, as in Job 38:7.

records.change: Omits "Into thine hand I commit my spirit"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text, which has the clause; Jesus speaks these words from the cross in Luke 23:46, and the CEV verse keeps only trust and rescue.

records.change: "The LORD imputeth not iniquity" becomes God forgiving confessed sins
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the Hebrew speaks of the LORD not reckoning sin, the wording Paul builds on in Romans 4:6-8. The CEV keeps forgiveness but not imputation.

records.change: "Anointed thee with the oil of gladness" becomes "chose you"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew mashach (anoint) is dropped, though Hebrews 1:8-9 applies the verse to Christ as the anointed one.

records.change: "He is thy Lord; worship thou him" becomes "do what he desires"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew hishtachavi means bow down, and the CEV makes the king her husband to be obeyed rather than a lord to be honoured.

records.change: Omits "for he shall receive me"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the CEV leaves it out and renders "the grave" as "death", losing the hope of being taken by God after death.

records.change: Sin from conception becomes sinning "since the day I was born"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the KJV's "shapen in iniquity" and "in sin did my mother conceive me", a text cited for original sin, become the psalmist's own sins from birth.

records.change: "Bloodguiltiness" becomes "any deadly sin"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew damim refers to guilt for shed blood, traditionally David's for Uriah, while the CEV turns it into a general plea to be kept from sin.

records.change: "Go down quick into hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew Sheol, as in 9:17; the CEV reads the realm of the dead where the KJV reads hell.

records.change: Drops "God most high" and "performeth all things for me"
records.note: The Masoretic text has both; the CEV compresses the verse to "my protector", losing the title Most High and the statement that God accomplishes all things for the psalmist.

records.change: Gifts come from enemies; "that the LORD God might dwell" lost
records.note: Translation choice on the Masoretic text. The KJV has gifts received for men, even the rebellious, so God may dwell among them; Ephesians 4:8 applies the verse to Christ's ascension.

records.change: "my people" brought back becomes "them" (the enemies)
records.note: The Hebrew has no object; the KJV supplies "my people" (restoration), the CEV reads it of enemies brought back for judgment, as the next verse suggests.

records.change: Princes coming to God becomes Egypt forced to bring bronze
records.note: A translation choice on an obscure Hebrew word ("princes" or "bronze"); the KJV's picture of Egypt and Ethiopia turning to God becomes forced tribute.

records.change: Omits "the king's son"
records.note: Translation choice on the Masoretic text; the CEV merges the parallel lines, dropping the royal son in a psalm often read messianically.

records.change: "he gave ear unto me" becomes a plea to listen
records.note: The Hebrew can be read as a statement (answered prayer) or a request; the KJV says God heard, the CEV only asks.

records.change: Omits "Turn us again" and "God of hosts"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the refrain's plea for restoration and the title; the CEV keeps only God's favour and salvation.

records.change: "son of man" and "man of thy right hand" rephrased away
records.note: Translation choice on the Masoretic text; the phrase "son of man", read messianically by some (the Targum names the King Messiah), no longer appears.

records.change: "their time... for ever" becomes "the end of them"
records.note: The Hebrew is obscure; the KJV has their time enduring for ever, the CEV reads it as their doom. A translation choice.

records.change: Omits the title "the living God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "the living God"; the CEV replaces it with "you", losing the title.

records.change: "thine anointed" becomes "I am your chosen one"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew mashiach (anointed) is made the psalmist, not a title that also points to the Messiah.

records.change: "the lowest hell" becomes "death and the grave"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol; the KJV renders it hell, the CEV death and the grave. A translation choice about the word, not the text.

records.change: "thy holy one" becomes "your faithful followers" (plural)
records.note: Hebrew manuscripts differ between singular and plural here; the KJV follows the singular, the CEV the plural.

records.change: "thine anointed" becomes "I am your chosen one"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew mashiach (anointed) is made the psalmist in first person rather than the anointed king.

records.change: "from everlasting to everlasting" becomes "always been God"
records.note: Translation choice; the CEV keeps God's eternity past but drops the explicit "to everlasting" future. Verse 4 still states it.

records.change: "the LORD our God is holy" becomes "Only you are God"
records.note: Translation choice on the Masoretic text; the psalm's refrain of God's holiness becomes a statement of his uniqueness.

records.change: Adds "Moses and Aaron" as those who obeyed
records.note: The Masoretic "they rebelled not" has an unclear subject (the Septuagint drops "not"); the CEV names Moses and Aaron as an interpretation.

records.change: Omits "the bread of heaven" (manna)
records.note: The Masoretic text has the bread of heaven; the CEV mentions only the quail. Manna is still described in Exodus 16 and Psalm 78:24.

records.change: Curses reframed as enemies' wishes; "from the LORD" dropped
records.note: Translation choice: the CEV reads verses 6-19 as the enemies' words, so the KJV's imprecation as a reward from the LORD is changed.

records.change: "the pains of hell" becomes "painful chains" of death
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol; the CEV folds it into death. A translation choice about the word, not the text.

records.change: "Precious... is the death of his saints" becomes "deeply concerned"
records.note: The Hebrew yaqar can mean precious or costly; the CEV reads it as God's concern, not the death being precious in his sight.

records.change: Word fixed for ever becomes lasting "as long as the heavens"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew says God's word stands fixed for ever in heaven, while the CEV moves "for ever" to God and ties the word's duration to the heavens. Its permanence is still stated in 119:152 and 119:160.

records.change: Priests clothed with "salvation" become robed in "victory"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew yesha can mean salvation or victory, and the CEV takes the military sense, narrowing the priestly picture of salvation.

records.change: "Magnified thy word above all thy name" becomes God's fame increasing
records.note: A long-disputed Masoretic phrase; the KJV sets God's word above his name, while the CEV follows the reading that God's faithfulness to his word made his name greater. The high view of God's word is lost here.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead, which the KJV renders "hell" here; God's presence everywhere is kept.

records.change: "The way everlasting" becomes "the way that time has proven true"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew derek olam can mean the everlasting or the ancient way, and the CEV takes the second, so the sense of an eternal way is lost.

records.change: "Beautify the meek with salvation" becomes "gives victory"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew yeshuah can mean salvation or victory, and the CEV takes the military sense.

records.change: Omits "I will pour out my spirit unto you"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; Wisdom's promise to pour out her spirit becomes "tell you what I think", losing the image some read alongside Joel 2:28.

records.change: "Covenant of her God" becomes "her wedding vows"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew speaks of the covenant of her God, and the CEV drops God, so marriage as a covenant made before God is not stated here.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol, the grave or realm of the dead, which the KJV renders "hell"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment.

records.change: "The way to hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment.

records.change: "The LORD possessed me" becomes "I was with the LORD"
records.note: The Hebrew qanah can mean possessed, acquired or created; the CEV avoids the verb. Many read Wisdom here as Christ, so the rendering was long debated.

records.change: "Set up from everlasting" becomes "the LORD gave life to me"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew nissakhti (set up, installed) is rendered as being given life, and "from everlasting" is dropped. Read of Christ, this makes Wisdom a created being, the question at the heart of the Arian dispute.

records.change: Guests "in the depths of hell" become "as good as dead"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell"; the CEV turns the place into a figure of speech, removing the sense of punishment.

records.change: "Hell and destruction" become "the world of the dead"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol and Abaddon; the CEV merges them into the realm of the dead, a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment.

records.change: "Hell beneath" becomes "death"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment.

records.change: Sin purged "by mercy and truth" becomes forgiven if we love God
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the Hebrew says iniquity is atoned for by mercy and truth, and the CEV makes forgiveness depend on our love for God.

records.change: "must shew himself friendly" becomes "Some friends don't help"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew verb is read by modern versions as "come to ruin" rather than "show oneself friendly", changing the first line's counsel.

records.change: "Deliver his soul from hell" becomes "save their lives"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell"; the CEV reads it as early death, a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment.

records.change: "The great God that formed all things" becomes an archer
records.note: The Hebrew is obscure; rab can mean a great one or an archer, and the CEV follows the second, as most modern versions do. God is not mentioned in its reading.

records.change: "Hell and destruction" become "death and the grave"
records.note: The Hebrew is Sheol and Abaddon, which the KJV renders "hell and destruction"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment.

records.change: "no vision" and "perish" become no guidance and lawlessness
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew chazon is prophetic revelation and para' means to run wild; the CEV makes the loss one of law and order rather than of the people perishing.

records.change: Pampered servant "become his son" becomes "cause you sorrow"
records.note: The Hebrew manon occurs only here and its meaning is uncertain; the KJV reads son or heir, the CEV grief.

records.change: Names "Ithiel and Ucal" become "I am completely worn out"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads personal names; the CEV follows a revocalisation of the Hebrew, as several modern versions do.

records.change: "His son's name" becomes "their children's names"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew is singular, his name and his son's name, asked of the one who made the world, which many read as pointing to the Son of God. The CEV's plural loses that.

records.change: "set the world in their heart" becomes questions about past and future
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew olam ("world", "eternity"); the CEV paraphrases it as questions about time rather than the world or eternity set in the heart.

records.change: Man's spirit going upward becomes a question: "if"
records.note: The Masoretic pointing reads "the spirit that goes upward", as the KJV has it; the CEV follows the ancient versions that read a question, so a spirit rising after death is left in doubt. Ecclesiastes 12:7 still says the spirit returns to God.

records.change: "The spirit" returning to God becomes "the life-giving breath"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew ruach means spirit or breath, and the CEV takes breath, which weakens the sense of the person's spirit returning to God.

records.change: "Hell hath enlarged herself" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is she'ol, the realm of the dead, which the CEV renders "world of the dead" where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "shall conceive" becomes "is pregnant"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew harah is an adjective read as present or future; the CEV's present tense weakens the sign as a future virgin conception, though "virgin" is kept and Matthew 1:23 applies it to Christ.

records.change: "Seek unto their God" becomes mediums urging "its own gods"
records.note: Translation choice: elohav can mean "their God" or "their gods"; the CEV puts the question in the mediums' mouths, so the prophet's call to seek God is lost here.

records.change: "Curse their king and their God" becomes "their gods"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew elohav can be read either way; the KJV reads the true God, the CEV idols.

records.change: "Not increased the joy" becomes people "are glad"
records.note: The written Hebrew (ketiv) has lo' "not"; the marginal reading (qere) has lo "to it". The KJV follows the ketiv, the CEV the qere, reversing the clause.

records.change: "Wells of salvation" becomes "well of victory"
records.note: Translation choice: yeshuah can mean salvation or victory; the CEV's word makes the deliverance military rather than spiritual.

records.change: "Hell from beneath" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is she'ol, the realm of the dead, which the CEV renders "world of the dead" where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "O Lucifer, son of the morning" becomes "bright morning star"
records.note: The Hebrew helel means "shining one"; the KJV follows the Vulgate's Lucifer, long read as a name of Satan. The CEV translates the word; the text is the same.

records.change: "Brought down to hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is she'ol, the realm of the dead, which the CEV renders "world of the dead" where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: Sluice and pond makers become weavers and paid workers
records.note: A translation choice on obscure Hebrew (shathoth, "foundations" or "weavers"); the CEV follows the reading as cloth workers.

records.change: "A saviour, and a great one" becomes "someone to rescue them"
records.note: Translation choice: the CEV drops "a great one" and the title saviour (moshia'), which some read messianically.

records.change: "Glorify ye the LORD in the fires" becomes "in the east"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew ba'urim ("in the fires" or "lights") is obscure; the CEV takes it as the region of sunrise.

records.change: "Precept upon precept" becomes "senseless sound after senseless sound"
records.note: Translation choice: the CEV reads tsav latsav as meaningless syllables mocking the prophet; the KJV reads them as the LORD's word given piece by piece.

records.change: "With hell are we at agreement" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is she'ol, the realm of the dead, which the CEV renders "world of the dead" where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: "Shall not make haste" becomes "will ever be disappointed"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "not hasten"; the CEV follows the sense of the Septuagint ("not be ashamed"), as quoted in Romans 9:33 and 1 Peter 2:6. The cornerstone is kept.

records.change: "Agreement with hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is she'ol, the realm of the dead, which the CEV renders "world of the dead" where the KJV renders it "hell".

records.change: Omits "the prophets" and "the seers" whom the LORD covered
records.note: The words are in the Masoretic text; some scholars take them as later glosses. The CEV leaves out who was blinded.

records.change: Omits "the Spirit of the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has ruach YHWH; the Septuagint has "the mind of the Lord", as Romans 11:34 quotes it. The CEV names only the LORD.

records.change: "Thou worm Jacob" becomes others calling Israel a worm
records.note: Translation choice: in the Hebrew the LORD himself calls Jacob a worm; the CEV moves the word to Israel's enemies. "Redeemer" becomes "saves and protects".

records.change: "Give thee for a covenant of the people" becomes "promise of hope"
records.note: Translation choice in a Servant Song: the Servant as himself the covenant (berit) is lost, a reading Christians apply to Christ.

records.change: "create evil" becomes "sorrow"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew ra, which can mean calamity as well as evil; the verse is often discussed on God's sovereignty over evil.

records.change: "Everlasting salvation" becomes "always keep you safe"
records.note: Translation choice: the CEV turns salvation into safety and drops "world without end"; eternal salvation is less explicit.

records.change: "I have chosen thee in the furnace" becomes "I tested you"
records.note: The Masoretic text has bachar "chosen"; the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) reads "tested", which the CEV follows or takes as the sense.

records.change: "Be my salvation" becomes "take my saving power"
records.note: Translation choice: the Servant who is God's salvation to the earth, quoted in Acts 13:47, becomes one who carries it.

records.change: Words to the despised one are addressed to Israel
records.note: Translation choice: the CEV reads the despised servant as Israel and adds "you are my chosen ones"; the KJV leaves the Servant, read as messianic, unnamed.

records.change: "Give thee for a covenant of the people" becomes "promise of hope"
records.note: As in 42:6, the Servant as the covenant itself is lost; a translation choice.

records.change: "land of Sinim" becomes "city of Syene"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads Sinim; the CEV follows the Dead Sea Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a), which reads Sewenim (Syene).

records.change: "See of the travail of his soul" becomes learning obedience by suffering
records.note: Translation choice in the Suffering Servant song: the Masoretic text has the Servant satisfied and justifying many by his knowledge. The Great Isaiah Scroll and Septuagint add "light". Bearing others' sins is kept.

records.change: "Their righteousness is of me" becomes "bless you with victory"
records.note: Translation choice: tsedaqah here, righteousness given by God, becomes victory; the idea of righteousness from God is lost.

records.change: "Debase thyself even unto hell" becomes consulting "spirits of the dead"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew is she'ol; the CEV also reads melek, "the king", as the god Molech.

records.change: "No intercessor" and salvation become "won victories for truth"
records.note: Translation choice: the intercessor (mapgia') and the salvation God's arm brought, often read messianically, are lost.

records.change: Omits "the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard"
records.note: The Hebrew is ambiguous; the CEV, like many modern versions, reads the flood as the LORD coming, driven by his wind (ruach), not the Spirit opposing an enemy.

records.change: Walls called "Salvation" become "Victory"
records.note: Translation choice: yeshuah can mean salvation or victory; the CEV's word makes the name military.

records.change: "Redeemer" from "everlasting" becomes "protector since ancient times"
records.note: Translation choice: go'el, redeemer, becomes protector, and God's everlasting name becomes his care since long ago.

records.change: "As if he slew a man" becomes sacrifice and murder together
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew sets the pairs side by side without "as if"; the KJV makes them comparisons, the CEV combined sins.

records.change: "Circumcise ... foreskins of your heart" becomes "keep the agreement"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew calls for circumcision of the heart, an image taken up in Deuteronomy 10:16 and Romans 2:29. The CEV keeps the call to wholehearted obedience but drops the figure.

records.change: "for ever and ever" becomes "a long life"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew promises dwelling in the land from age to age. The CEV narrows the lasting promise to one long lifetime.

records.change: "understandeth and knoweth me" becomes "worshiping me"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew speaks of understanding and knowing the LORD, the verse Paul echoes in 1 Corinthians 1:31. The CEV makes the boast one of worship, and renders "righteousness" as "mercy".

records.change: "a righteous Branch" becomes "an honest king"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew tsemach (Branch) is a messianic title also used in Jeremiah 33:15 and Zechariah 3:8 and 6:12. The CEV keeps a king from David's family but drops the title and weakens "righteous" to "honest".

records.change: "THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS" becomes "The LORD Gives Justice"
records.note: A translation choice on the name YHWH tsidqenu; the messianic king's title naming the LORD as our righteousness becomes a statement about justice.

records.change: King "Jehoiakim" becomes "Zedekiah"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads Jehoiakim; the CEV follows a few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac, which read Zedekiah to agree with 27:3, 27:12 and 28:1. The Septuagint lacks the verse.

records.change: "David their king" becomes "a king ... from the family of David"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew names the coming king "David", read messianically as in Ezekiel 34:23-24 and Hosea 3:5. The CEV keeps a Davidic king but loses the name.

records.change: "Ephraim is my firstborn" becomes "my favorite children"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew names Ephraim as God's firstborn, a covenant title of rank and inheritance. The CEV drops both Ephraim and "firstborn".

records.change: "Created a new thing" becomes a comparison: "as different as"
records.note: A translation choice on an obscure Masoretic line, a woman shall encompass a man; the CEV makes the new creation a figure of change, dropping the reading some older interpreters took of the incarnation.

records.change: "I was an husband unto them" becomes "I was their God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has ba'alti, I was husband or master to them (the Septuagint and Hebrews 8:9 read I disregarded them); the CEV drops the marriage picture of the covenant.

records.change: "Know the LORD" and "all know me" become "obey me"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew yada' is to know, the personal knowledge of God promised in the new covenant (quoted in Hebrews 8:11), which the CEV turns into obedience.

records.change: Omits the title "the Great, the Mighty God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has ha'el haggadol haggibbor; the CEV keeps only "LORD All-Powerful". El Gibbor is the title given the promised child in Isaiah 9:6.

records.change: Jehudi's ancestor Shelemiah made a second messenger
records.note: The Hebrew gives Jehudi's lineage, son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi; the CEV sends "Jehudi and Shelemiah", two men, a reading the text does not support.

records.change: No one will swear by God's name becomes God refusing their promises
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew says God's name will no more be named by any man of Judah in Egypt (for none will be left, 44:27), which the CEV makes a refusal to accept their vows.

records.change: "Thy valiant men swept away" becomes striking down "your mighty god Apis"
records.note: The CEV follows the Septuagint, which divides the Hebrew nischaph as nas Chaph, Apis has fled; the Masoretic text reads why are thy valiant ones swept away, in the plural.

records.change: "Brought forth our righteousness" becomes "taken revenge"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew tsidqotenu is our righteousness or vindication, God's showing his people in the right, which the CEV turns into vengeance on Babylon.

records.change: Omits "whither the spirit was to go" guiding the creatures
records.note: The Masoretic text says the creatures went wherever the ruach, the spirit, would go, often read as God's Spirit directing them; the CEV explains their movement by their facing forward instead.

records.change: "New spirit" and "heart of flesh" become eagerness to be faithful
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the promise of one heart, a new spirit and a heart of flesh for a stony one, read as inward renewal, is reduced to a change of attitude. The same promise is stated in full in Ezekiel 36:26.

records.change: "Make you a new heart and a new spirit" becomes "thinking pure thoughts"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the call to a new heart and spirit, read as inward renewal, becomes a change of thinking. The promise itself is kept in full in Ezekiel 36:26.

records.change: "I am the LORD that sanctify them" becomes "they were holy"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew names the LORD as the one who makes Israel holy (meqaddesh), while the CEV makes the Sabbath show that they were holy, so God's sanctifying act is lost here.

records.change: Omits "the rod of my son"; becomes "ignored my warnings"
records.note: The Hebrew of this clause is obscure and translations differ widely; the CEV's paraphrase drops the "son" and his rod (sceptre), which some read with Genesis 49:10 as a royal or messianic allusion.

records.change: The king is no longer "the anointed cherub"; a cherub guards him
records.note: The CEV follows the Septuagint (and a revocalised Hebrew, 'et for 'att), where the king is with a cherub, rather than the Masoretic text, where he is the cherub. The verse is often read of Satan's fall, which this reading removes.

records.change: "Destroy thee, O covering cherub" becomes the cherub chasing him away
records.note: As in 28:14, the CEV follows the Septuagint reading in which the cherub expels the king, where the Masoretic text addresses the king himself as the covering cherub.

records.change: Challenging questions become Sheba and Dedan as "your allies"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the nations question Gog's plunder; the CEV reads them as allies wanting a share, and drops "the young lions".

records.change: "Like the Son of God" becomes "looks like a god"
records.note: A translation choice; the Aramaic bar-elahin can mean "a son of the gods", as Nebuchadnezzar might say, and most modern versions read so. The KJV's capitalised reading supports the view that the fourth figure was a pre-incarnate appearance of Christ, which the CEV rules out.

records.change: "The army of heaven" becomes "the stars in the sky"
records.note: A translation choice; the Aramaic "host of heaven" can mean the angels as well as the stars, and the CEV narrows it to the stars, so God's rule over the heavenly beings is not stated.

records.change: Drops "servant of the living God"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Aramaic; the king's title for God as "the living God", repeated in verse 26, is left out here.

records.change: Thrones "cast down" become "set up"; "Ancient of days" becomes "Eternal God"
records.note: A translation choice: the Aramaic remah can mean "thrown" or "placed"; the title "Ancient of days" is paraphrased.

records.change: "The Son of man" becomes "a son of man"
records.note: The Aramaic is "one like a son of man", so the lower case is a fair translation, but it drops the title Jesus took from this verse (Matthew 26:64). "Ancient of days" is also rendered "the Eternal God".

records.change: Drops "reconciliation for iniquity"; "anoint the most Holy" becomes a place
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the atonement clause becomes the people suffering "as the price of their sins", and "a most holy place will be dedicated" takes the anointing as a temple, not the Messiah. The Hebrew "most holy" can mean either.

records.change: "Messiah the Prince" becomes "the Chosen Leader"
records.note: The Hebrew mashiach nagid is "an anointed one, a prince"; the CEV's "Chosen Leader" keeps a single figure but drops "anointed", the word behind "Messiah" and "Christ".

records.change: "Messiah cut off, but not for himself" becomes "Chosen Leader killed"
records.note: A translation choice; "left with nothing" is a fair reading of the Hebrew ve'ein lo, but it drops the KJV's sense that he died not for his own sake, read as a prophecy of Christ's death for others.

records.change: "he" becomes "this foreigner"
records.note: The Aramaic has only "he"; the CEV names him a foreign ruler, settling a disputed prophecy that some read of the Messiah confirming the covenant.

records.change: "The God of his fathers" becomes "the gods his ancestors worshiped"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew elohim can be singular or plural. The plural rules out the reading that this king turns from Israel's God.

records.change: Drops "for ever and ever"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the wise shine like the stars, but the verse no longer says it lasts forever.

records.change: "like men" becomes "At a place named Adam"
records.note: A translation choice, often with a slight emendation of the Hebrew ke'adam ("like Adam" or "like men") to a place name.

records.change: Judah faithful to God becomes "Judah worships other gods"
records.note: A translation choice on obscure Hebrew; the CEV reverses the KJV's praise of Judah and reads "the saints" as God himself.

records.change: "Call on the name of the LORD" becomes "faithfully worships him"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; calling on the LORD's name, quoted in Acts 2:21 and Romans 10:13, is made a matter of faithful worship.

records.change: "Cleanse their blood" becomes "punish the guilty and defend the innocent"
records.note: The Hebrew niqqeti means "I will acquit" or "hold innocent"; the CEV's punishing sense is closer to the Septuagint's "I will avenge their blood".

records.change: "The house of their god" becomes "my temple"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew elohehem can be "their god" or "their God". The KJV reads idolatry, the CEV the LORD's own house profaned.

records.change: "Moloch and Chiun" becomes the idols "Sakkuth" and "Kaiwan"; made future
records.note: The CEV reads the Masoretic consonants as the names of Assyrian star gods; the KJV follows older renderings close to the Septuagint that Stephen quotes in Acts 7:43. The CEV also makes the past "have borne" a future threat.

records.change: "Forgive, I beseech thee" becomes "Forgive me for asking"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; Amos's plea for God to forgive Israel becomes an apology for his own question, so his intercession is lost.

records.change: "Thy god, O Dan" becomes vows "in my name" at Dan
records.note: The CEV reads the Hebrew ashmat "sin" as the goddess Ashimah, and turns the oath by Dan's god into oaths by the LORD, reversing the KJV's idolatry at Dan.

records.change: "Dig into hell" becomes "dig deep into the earth"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead; the verse's point, that none can hide from God, is kept.

records.change: Drops "the house of Joseph a flame"
