records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; Jacob and Joseph are merged into "Israel", so the northern tribes' part in Edom's judgment is not stated.

records.change: "The belly of hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew Sheol, the grave or realm of the dead; Jonah's cry from near death is kept.

records.change: "The breaker" and "their king" merged into "I"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; the one who breaks out ahead and the king at the head of the people, often read messianically, become the LORD alone.

records.change: "From everlasting" becomes "family goes back to ancient times"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew "from of old, from days of eternity" can mean ancient descent from David, but the KJV reads it as the ruler's eternal origin. Matthew 2:6 applies the verse to Christ.

records.change: "the just shall live by his faith" becomes "acceptable to me"
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text; "the just" and "shall live" are lost in a verse quoted in Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11 and Hebrews 10:38, though faith is kept.

records.change: "Enlargeth his desire as hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew Sheol, the realm of the dead, pictured here as never satisfied.

records.change: "Thine anointed" becomes "your chosen one"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew mashiach is "anointed", which the CEV renders "chosen one", losing the word behind "Messiah".

records.change: "the desire of all nations shall come" becomes "their treasures"
records.note: The Masoretic noun (chemdat) is singular with a plural verb; the KJV reads a person, long taken as messianic, while the CEV takes it as the nations' wealth. A translation choice, but the messianic reading is lost.

records.change: "the LORD of hosts hath sent me" becomes "I am a prophet"
records.note: The Hebrew has the LORD speaking of being sent by the LORD of hosts, read by many as a hint of a divine Sent One; the CEV makes the speaker the prophet. A translation choice.

records.change: "The LORD rebuke thee" becomes "Satan, you are wrong"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the LORD invoking the LORD's rebuke (echoed in Jude 9); the CEV turns it into a plain contradiction. A translation choice that drops the rebuke formula.

records.change: "seven eyes" on the stone becomes "seven sides"
records.note: The Hebrew word is "eyes"; the CEV reads it as facets. A translation choice that changes the image in a messianic passage (the stone and the Branch of 3:8).

records.change: "a priest upon his throne" becomes a priest beside his throne
records.note: The Masoretic text makes the Branch both king and priest; the CEV follows the Septuagint's "a priest at his right hand", making two persons. The king-priest union, applied to Christ in Hebrews, is lost here. Joined with 6:12 in the CEV.

records.change: "Helem" and "Hen" become "Heldai" and "Josiah"; one crown
records.note: The CEV harmonises the names with 6:10, following the Syriac, where the Masoretic text has Helem and Hen; it also reads the plural "crowns" as one crown.

records.change: Omits "he is just"; "having salvation" becomes "has won a victory"
records.note: The Hebrew calls the coming king righteous (tsaddiq) and saved or victorious (nosha); the CEV drops "just" and reads victory. Quoted of Christ in Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15; his lowliness is kept.

records.change: Omits "the house of David shall be as God"
records.note: The Masoretic text says David's house will be "as God (elohim), as the angel of the LORD"; the CEV keeps only the angel. A translation choice that softens the comparison.

records.change: "look upon me whom they have pierced" becomes "the one they pierced"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "upon me", the LORD himself pierced; some Hebrew manuscripts and John 19:37 read "him", which the CEV follows. It also drops "the spirit of grace"; the messianic application stays.

records.change: Omits "wounds in thine hands"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "between your hands" is read by modern versions as the chest or back; the CEV drops the hands, often read as messianic.

records.change: Omits "that have no rain"
records.note: The Masoretic text is difficult here (literally "not upon them"); the Septuagint and some Hebrew manuscripts drop the "not", and the CEV leaves the rain out. A textual and translation difficulty with little doctrinal weight.

records.change: Adds a condition: angry "as long as they are so sinful"
records.note: The Hebrew says the LORD has indignation against Edom for ever (ad olam); the CEV adds a condition the text does not state. A translation choice that softens the lasting judgment.

records.change: Future "shall be great among the Gentiles" becomes present "is praised"
records.note: The Hebrew clause has no verb, so the tense is the translator's choice; the KJV reads a prophecy of the Gentiles' worship, the CEV a present fact.

records.change: Omits marrying "the daughter of a strange god"; makes it idolatry
records.note: The Hebrew speaks of marrying foreign women who worship other gods; the CEV keeps only the worship of other gods and loses the marriage, which the passage goes on to address.

records.change: God hating "putting away" becomes hating the man who divorces
records.note: The Hebrew is ambiguous ("he hates sending away" or "one who hates and divorces"); the KJV has God hating divorce itself, the CEV the cruel husband. A translation choice.

records.change: Drops the angel's address "thou son of David"
records.note: The Greek of every text-type has "son of David"; the CEV leaves it out as a paraphrase. Joseph's Davidic line is still given in Matthew 1:6-16.

records.change: Omits "her firstborn son"; says only "her baby was born"
records.note: "Firstborn" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, which the CEV follows. Luke 2:7 still calls Jesus Mary's firstborn.

records.change: Omits "without a cause"
records.note: The qualifier is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or some early fathers; without it all anger is condemned, not only unjust anger.

records.change: Omits "bless them that curse you" and "do good to them"
records.note: These clauses and "despitefully use you" are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Luke 6:27-28 has the same commands.

records.change: Omits "openly" from the Father's reward
records.note: "En to phanero" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The promise of reward remains.

records.change: Omits the doxology "For thine is the kingdom… for ever. Amen"
records.note: The doxology is in the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or the early Latin and Greek commentators. Similar praise is in 1 Chronicles 29:11.

records.change: Omits "openly" from the Father's reward
records.note: As in 6:6, "openly" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits the disciples' address "Lord"
records.note: "Kyrie" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Jesus is called Lord throughout Matthew.

records.change: Omits "draweth nigh unto me with their mouth"
records.note: The clause, from Isaiah 29:13, is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The sense is kept by "honoureth me with their lips".

records.change: "The gates of hell" becomes "death itself"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek is "gates of Hades", the realm of the dead, which the KJV renders "hell". The promise that the church will stand is kept.

records.change: Omits the verse: casting out "by prayer and fasting"
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the CEV gives it in a footnote. Mark 9:29 has a similar saying.

records.change: Omits the verse: the Son of man came to save the lost
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or early versions; it may come from Luke 19:10, where the same words stand.

records.change: "Seventy times seven" becomes "seventy-seven times"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "hebdomekontakis hepta" can mean either, and Genesis 4:24 (LXX) uses it for seventy-seven. The point, unlimited forgiveness, is kept.

records.change: "Why callest thou me good?" becomes "Why ask me about what is good?"
records.note: The critical text (Sinaiticus, Vaticanus) reads "Why do you ask me about the good?"; the Textus Receptus agrees with Mark 10:18 and Luke 18:19, where the question about Jesus being called good is still stated.

records.change: Omits "for many be called, but few chosen"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The same saying stands in Matthew 22:14.

records.change: Omits "to be baptized with the baptism" clause
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or D; it is still stated in Mark 10:38.

records.change: Omits "be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with"
records.note: The clause, here and in 20:22, is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Mark 10:38-39 has it.

records.change: "The temple of God" becomes "the temple"
records.note: "Tou theou" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Which temple is meant is plain.

records.change: Omits "even Christ" as the one Master
records.note: "Ho Christos" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Verse 10 still names Christ as the one teacher.

records.change: Omits the verse: woe for devouring widows' houses
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Bezae. The same woe stands in Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47.

records.change: Adds "the Son himself doesn't know"
records.note: "Neither the Son" is in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and D but not in the Byzantine majority or Textus Receptus; the same words are in all texts of Mark 13:32.

records.change: Omits "wherein the Son of man cometh"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Christ's coming is plain from 24:44 and 25:31.

records.change: "This just person" becomes "this man"
records.note: "Tou dikaiou" is in the Byzantine text, the Textus Receptus and Sinaiticus but not in Vaticanus or Bezae. Christ's innocence is still stated in 27:4 and 27:19.

records.change: Omits the fulfilment of "They parted my garments… cast lots"
records.note: The quotation of Psalm 22:18 is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or the Byzantine majority. John 19:24 cites the same fulfilment.

records.change: "Where the Lord lay" becomes "where his body was lying"
records.note: "Ho Kyrios" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The resurrection is stated in full.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Bezae.

records.change: "the prophets" becomes "Isaiah the prophet"
records.note: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early witnesses read "in Isaiah the prophet"; the Byzantine text reads "in the prophets", since the quotation joins Malachi 3:1 with Isaiah 40:3.

records.change: Omits "to heal sicknesses"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The apostles' healing is recorded in Mark 6:13.

records.change: "Eternal damnation" becomes a sin held against you forever
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "eternal judgment" (kriseos), Sinaiticus and Vaticanus "eternal sin" (hamartematos), which the CEV follows. Both state an unforgivable, lasting guilt.

records.change: Omits "more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment"
records.note: The sentence is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Bezae. The same warning stands in Matthew 10:15.

records.change: Omits "as the washing of pots and cups…"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Mark 7:4 describes the same washings.

records.change: Verse omitted; its number points to the verse before
records.note: The CEV leaves this verse out with Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; it is in the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus.

records.change: Omits "nor tell it to any in the town"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The command not to enter the village remains.

records.change: "If thou canst believe" becomes "Why do you say 'if you can'?"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "pisteusai" (to believe); Sinaiticus and Vaticanus lack it, so Jesus repeats the father's "if you can". The call to faith remains.

records.change: Omits the address "Lord" and "with tears"
records.note: "Kyrie" and "meta dakryon" are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "and fasting"; only prayer casts out this kind
records.note: "Kai nesteia" is in the Byzantine text, the Textus Receptus and most witnesses but not in the first hand of Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Fasting is still taught in Matthew 6:16-18.

records.change: Verse omitted; its number points to the verse before
records.note: The CEV leaves this verse out with Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; it is in the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus. The same words stand in 9:48.

records.change: Verse omitted; its number points to the verse before
records.note: The CEV leaves this verse out with Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; it is in the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus. The same words stand in 9:48.

records.change: Omits "every sacrifice shall be salted with salt"
records.note: The clause is in the Textus Receptus and Byzantine witnesses (from Leviticus 2:13) but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and some others; the CEV follows the latter.

records.change: Omits "take up the cross"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early witnesses. Taking up the cross is still taught in Mark 8:34.

records.change: Omits "for them that trust in riches"
records.note: The qualifier is in most manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus. Without it the saying is about entering the kingdom at all, not about the rich.

records.change: Omits "that cometh in the name of the Lord"
records.note: The repeated phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the Alexandrian witnesses the CEV follows; it is still in verse 9.

records.change: Verse omitted: Father will not forgive the unforgiving
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others; the CEV joins it to verse 25 without its words. The same teaching is in Matthew 6:15.

records.change: Omits "at him they cast stones"
records.note: The stoning is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early witnesses.

records.change: Omits "this is the first commandment"
records.note: The closing words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; verse 28-29 still name it the first commandment.

records.change: Omits "but he answered nothing"
records.note: The clause is found in some later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in most witnesses; Jesus' silence is still told in verses 4-5.

records.change: Verse omitted: Isaiah's "numbered with the transgressors" fulfilled
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others; the CEV joins it to verse 27 without its words. The fulfilment of Isaiah 53:12 is still cited in Luke 22:37.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The Amen is in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in most witnesses to the longer ending.

records.change: Omits "blessed art thou among women"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; Elisabeth still says them in verse 42.

records.change: "good will toward men" becomes peace to "everyone who pleases God"
records.note: The critical text reads eudokias ("among people of his good pleasure") with Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Byzantine text reads eudokia, goodwill offered to all people.

records.change: "the Lord's Christ" becomes "Christ the Lord"
records.note: The Greek is the same in all texts (the Lord's anointed); the CEV's rendering is a translation choice that turns "the Lord" from God the Father into a title of Christ.

records.change: "Joseph and his mother" becomes "Jesus' parents"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Joseph and his mother"; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and the critical text read "his father and mother", which the CEV gives as "parents". The virgin birth is still plain in Luke 1:34-35.

records.change: Omits "in spirit"
records.note: "In spirit" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; it may come from Luke 1:80.

records.change: "Joseph and his mother" becomes "his parents"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Joseph and his mother"; the Alexandrian witnesses and the critical text read "his parents". Luke also says "his parents" in 2:41 in all texts.

records.change: "Aram" becomes "Admin, Arni", adding a name
records.note: The critical text follows manuscripts reading Admin and Arni where the Textus Receptus has Aram (as in Matthew 1:3-4 and Ruth 4:19).

records.change: Omits "but by every word of God"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; it is still in Matthew 4:4.

records.change: Omits "Get thee behind me, Satan"
records.note: The rebuke is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in the early Alexandrian witnesses; it is in Matthew 4:10.

records.change: Omits "to heal the brokenhearted"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or D; it is in the source, Isaiah 61:1.

records.change: Omits "Christ" from "Thou art Christ the Son of God"
records.note: "The Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the Alexandrian witnesses; the verse still calls him the Messiah at its end.

records.change: Omits "and both are preserved"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; it is in Matthew 9:17.

records.change: Omits "prophet": no one greater than John
records.note: "Prophet" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the Alexandrian witnesses; without it John is said to be greater than anyone born of women.

records.change: Omits "Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of"
records.note: The saying is in many later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early witnesses; only the rebuke remains.

records.change: Omits "the Son of man is not come to destroy... save"
records.note: The sentence belongs with the addition in verse 55 and is absent from the same early witnesses. Christ coming to save is still stated in Luke 19:10.

records.change: Omits the address "Lord"
records.note: "Lord" is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in the Alexandrian witnesses.

records.change: Omits "which art in heaven" and "Thy will be done"
records.note: Luke's prayer is shorter in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and the critical text; the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have the fuller form, as in Matthew 6:9-10.

records.change: Omits "but deliver us from evil"
records.note: Luke's shorter form of the Lord's Prayer follows Sinaiticus (corrected), Vaticanus and early papyri; the petition is still stated in Matthew 6:13.

records.change: Omits the bread-and-stone question
records.note: The bread and stone clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in some early witnesses; it is in Matthew 7:9.

records.change: Verse omitted: two men in the field
records.note: The verse is in some Western and later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and most witnesses; it is thought to come from Matthew 24:40, where it stands in all texts. The CEV joins it to verse 35 without its words.

records.change: Omits "unto the offerings of God"
records.note: "Of God" is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the CEV paraphrase leaves out the offerings altogether. The sense of the widow's gift is unchanged.

records.change: "the Lord said" becomes "Jesus said"
records.note: "And the Lord said" is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P75, Vaticanus or Sinaiticus; the CEV supplies the name. The title "Lord" is lost here only.

records.change: Omits "they struck him on the face"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the striking is still implied in "who struck you" and stated in Matthew 26:67.

records.change: Omits "nor let me go"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Only a detail of Jesus' reply is lost.

records.change: Verse omitted; the custom of a festival release not stated
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P75, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; verse 16 does not carry its words. The custom is still stated in Matthew 27:15 and Mark 15:6.

records.change: Omits "in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P75, Vaticanus or Sinaiticus (first hand); the three languages are still stated in John 19:20.

records.change: Omits the thief's address "Lord"
records.note: The Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus read "Lord, remember me"; P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "Jesus, remember me". The thief's acknowledgement of Christ as Lord is weakened.

records.change: Omits "and certain others with them"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; other women are still named in verse 10.

records.change: Omits "and of an honeycomb"
records.note: The honeycomb is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. Only a detail of the meal is lost.

records.change: Omits "blessing" and the closing "Amen"
records.note: "Praising and blessing" and "Amen" are in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus; P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have one verb and no "Amen". The sense is unchanged.

records.change: "only begotten of the Father" becomes "only Son of the Father"
records.note: A translation choice on monogenes, read as "only" or "unique" rather than "only begotten"; the Greek is the same in both texts. Christ's sonship is kept, the begetting is not expressed.

records.change: "only begotten Son" becomes "only Son, who is truly God"
records.note: P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "only God" (monogenes theos), the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus "only begotten Son"; the CEV combines both. Christ's deity is stated more directly, not less.

records.change: Omits "which is in heaven"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine majority, Alexandrinus and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; it states the Son is in heaven while speaking on earth.

records.change: "only begotten Son" becomes "only Son"
records.note: A translation choice on monogenes, read as "only" or "unique"; the Greek is the same in both texts. The begetting of the Son is not expressed.

records.change: "only begotten Son of God" becomes "God's only Son"
records.note: A translation choice on monogenes, as in John 3:16; the Greek is the same in both texts.

records.change: "the Lord knew" becomes "Jesus knew"
records.note: The Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus read "the Lord"; Sinaiticus, D and some others read "Jesus". Only the title is lost here.

records.change: Omits "the Christ" before "the Saviour of the world"
records.note: "The Christ" is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; Jesus is still called Saviour of the world.

records.change: Omits "waiting for the moving of the water"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; it prepares for verse 4, also missing.

records.change: Verse omitted; the angel stirring the pool not stated
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine majority, Alexandrinus and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; verse 3 does not carry its words. The sick man's words in verse 7 still assume it.

records.change: "Christ, the Son of the living God" becomes "God's Holy One"
records.note: P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "the Holy One of God"; the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus read "the Christ, the Son of the living God". Peter's confession of Christ as Son is still in Matthew 16:16.

records.change: "a devil" becomes "a demon"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek is diabolos (devil, slanderer), not daimonion (demon), in both texts. The CEV names a different kind of being.

records.change: "I go not up yet" becomes "I am not going"
records.note: The Byzantine majority, P66, P75 and Vaticanus read "not yet" (oupo); Sinaiticus and D read "not" (ouk). Without "yet", Jesus' going up in verse 10 can read as a change of mind.

records.change: Omits "being convicted by their own conscience"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in D or most witnesses that carry the passage. Only the reason for their leaving is lost.

records.change: Omits "saw none but the woman"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in D or many witnesses that carry the passage. The sense is unchanged.

records.change: "Neither do I condemn thee" becomes "not going to accuse you"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek katakrino means condemn, a verdict, not accuse. The CEV reading loses Jesus' judgment of pardon.

records.change: Omits "going through the midst of them, and so passed by"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus (first hand) or Vaticanus. Only the manner of his escape is lost.

records.change: "the Son of God" becomes "the Son of Man"
records.note: P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "Son of Man"; the Byzantine majority, Alexandrinus and Textus Receptus read "Son of God". The man's worship in verse 38 follows either reading.

records.change: Omits "as I said unto you"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine majority, Alexandrinus and Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The sense is unchanged.

records.change: Adds that Mary poured perfume on the Lord's "head"
records.note: The CEV joins this verse to verse 1 and adds "head", which no Greek text has here; John 12:3 has her anoint his feet. The anointing of the head is in Matthew 26:7 and Mark 14:3.

records.change: Omits "Simon's son"
records.note: "Simon's son" is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; Judas is called Simon's son in John 6:71 and 13:2.

records.change: "hear my words, and believe not" becomes "refuse to obey my teachings"
records.note: The Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus read "believe not" (pisteuse); P66, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others read "keep them not" (phulaxe). Faith is replaced by obedience here.

records.change: Omits "in my name"
records.note: "In my name" is in every Greek text; the CEV leaves it out here and in verse 13, following the critical text's added "me". Asking in Christ's name is still stated in John 15:16 and 16:23.

records.change: Omits "because I go to the Father"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P5, P66, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the disciples still quote it in verse 17.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. The sense is unchanged.

records.change: "my soul in hell" becomes "me in the grave"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek is hades in both texts, which the KJV renders "hell" and the CEV "the grave". The resurrection reading is kept.

records.change: Omits raising up "Christ" "according to the flesh"; "someone" becomes king
records.note: "According to the flesh, he would raise up Christ" is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; the CEV's "someone" leaves the promise unnamed here, though verse 31 names Christ.

records.change: "his soul was not left in hell" becomes "in the grave"
records.note: A translation choice on hades, as in verse 27; the Byzantine text also has "his soul", which the critical text and the CEV lack.

records.change: "his Son Jesus" becomes "his Servant Jesus"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek pais means child or servant in both texts, and echoes Isaiah's Servant. The KJV reads sonship, the CEV servanthood; Christ is still called Son in Acts 9:20 and 13:33.

records.change: "Lord, thou art God" becomes "Master"
records.note: "Thou art God" (ho theos) is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. God is still addressed as Creator.

records.change: "an angel of the Lord" becomes "an angel"
records.note: "Of the Lord" is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; the Lord's voice is still stated in verse 31.

records.change: Omits "him shall ye hear"
records.note: The command is in C, E and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus or the Byzantine majority; it is still in Deuteronomy 18:15 and Acts 3:22.

records.change: "for the God of Jacob" becomes "for the people of Israel"
records.note: The Byzantine majority, Alexandrinus and Textus Receptus read "for the God of Jacob"; P74, Sinaiticus (first hand), Vaticanus and D read "for the house of Jacob". The dwelling is for the people rather than God.

records.change: Omits the verse: the eunuch confesses Jesus as Son of God
records.note: The verse is in the Textus Receptus and some Western witnesses but not in the early Greek manuscripts; the CEV's 8:36 has no confession. Jesus as Son of God is still stated in Acts 9:20.

records.change: Omits "it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks"
records.note: The clause is in the Textus Receptus (from the Latin) but not in the Greek manuscripts here; it is present in all texts at Acts 26:14.

records.change: Omits Saul's trembling question "Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?"
records.note: The words came into the Textus Receptus from the Latin and are not in the Greek manuscripts here; Paul's question is in all texts at Acts 22:10.

records.change: "preached Christ" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The critical text reads "Jesus" where the Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; he is still called the Son of God.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: The critical text reads "the Lord" without "Jesus"; the CEV moves the phrase into 9:28. Only the name differs.

records.change: Omits "he shall tell thee what thou oughtest to do"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows. Similar words stand in Acts 11:14.

records.change: Omits Cornelius's "fasting"; he was only praying
records.note: "Fasting" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the early manuscripts or the critical text. Fasting with prayer is still found in Acts 13:3 and 14:23.

records.change: Omits "who, when he cometh, shall speak unto thee"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows.

records.change: "the name of the Lord" becomes "Jesus Christ"
records.note: The critical text reads "Jesus Christ" where the Textus Receptus reads "the Lord"; the translation names Christ more fully, not less.

records.change: "my Son...begotten thee" becomes "my son...become your Father"
records.note: A translation choice for Psalm 2:7: the CEV writes "son" in lower case and renders "begotten" as becoming Father. The sonship is kept; the capital and "begotten" are not.

records.change: Gentiles "hear...and believe" becomes "hear and obey him"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek reads "believe" (pisteusai). Obeying for believing shifts what the Gentiles were called to.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: The critical text omits "Christ", which the Textus Receptus has. Salvation by grace is still stated.

records.change: Omits "Known unto God are all his works"
records.note: The critical text reads only "known from of old" as the end of the quotation; the Textus Receptus adds "unto God are all his works". God's foreknowledge of his works drops out.

records.change: Omits "Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows. The dispute is still stated in Acts 15:1 and 15:5.

records.change: Verse omitted; Silas staying in Antioch not stated
records.note: The verse is missing from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority but is in the Textus Receptus; the CEV gives verse 35's words here.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: The critical text omits "Christ". Faith in the Lord Jesus for salvation is kept.

records.change: "of one blood" becomes "from one person"
records.note: The critical text omits "blood" (haimatos), reading "from one". The unity of mankind is kept either way.

records.change: God "winked at" ignorance becomes God "forgave" it
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek means God overlooked those times, not that he forgave them; the call to repent ("turn to him") remains.

records.change: "pressed in the spirit" becomes occupied with preaching
records.note: The critical text reads "pressed by the word" where the Textus Receptus reads "in the spirit"; the CEV follows the former.

records.change: Omits "I must by all means keep this feast...in Jerusalem"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows. His sailing from Ephesus is also left out of this verse.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The critical text omits "Christ" here. Jesus is still the one John pointed to.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: The critical text omits "Jesus"; only the name differs.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: Some early manuscripts omit "Christ" and the CEV follows them. Faith toward the Lord Jesus is kept.

records.change: "his own blood" becomes "the blood of his own Son"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "dia tou haimatos tou idiou" can be read "his own blood" or "the blood of his own one"; the KJV reading names God's own blood, pointing to Christ's deity.

records.change: Omits "that they observe no such thing, save only"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows. The four rules themselves are kept.

records.change: Omits "and were afraid"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows.

records.change: Omits "let us not fight against God"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows. The Pharisees' defence of Paul is otherwise kept.

records.change: Omits the verse about Lysias taking Paul by force
records.note: Acts 24:6b-8a is in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in the early ones; the CEV's 24:6 has none of it.

records.change: Omits "Commanding his accusers to come unto thee"
records.note: Part of the same Textus Receptus passage (24:6b-8a); the rest of the verse is kept in the CEV's 24:6.

records.change: Omits the centurion handing over the prisoners
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows.

records.change: Omits the verse: the Jews departed, reasoning among themselves
records.note: The verse is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in the early ones; the CEV's 28:28 does not carry it.

records.change: "the gospel of Christ" becomes "the good news"
records.note: The critical text omits "of Christ". The gospel as God's power to save is kept.

records.change: "eternal power and Godhead" becomes "power and character"
records.note: A translation choice for theiotes, "divine nature"; "character" loses the sense of deity.

records.change: "a Jew, which is one inwardly" becomes "you must obey the Law"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek says the true Jew is one inwardly, in the spirit. The CEV's first sentence makes obeying the Law the mark instead.

records.change: Omits "by faith" from access into grace
records.note: Some early manuscripts lack "by faith" and the critical text brackets it. Justification by faith is still stated in 5:1.

records.change: Omits "our Lord" after "Jesus Christ"
records.note: The critical text reads "in Christ Jesus" without "our Lord".

records.change: Omits "who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows. The same words stand in all texts at 8:4.

records.change: "the firstborn among many brethren" becomes "the first of many"
records.note: A translation choice: prototokos carries rank and pre-eminence, which "first" does not; Christ is still "firstborn" elsewhere, e.g. Colossians 1:15 in other versions.

records.change: "the word of God" becomes "the message about Christ"
records.note: The critical text reads "the word of Christ" where the Textus Receptus reads "of God".

records.change: Omits "if it be of works, then is it no more grace"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows. The first half, grace not of works, is kept.

records.change: Omits "he that regardeth not the day...doth not regard it"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the earliest Greek manuscripts or the critical text, which the CEV follows.

records.change: "judgment seat of Christ" becomes "God will judge"
records.note: The critical text reads "judgment seat of God"; Christ as judge is still stated in 2 Corinthians 5:10.

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The critical text omits "Jesus" here; only the name differs.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ the Lord"
records.note: The critical text omits "Jesus"; only the name differs.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ...Amen" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: The critical text omits "Christ" and "Amen" in the benediction.

records.change: Omits the verse: the benediction "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ"
records.note: The verse is in the Textus Receptus and later manuscripts but not in the early ones; the CEV's 16:23 lacks it. The same blessing stands in 16:20.

records.change: "Christ the power of God" becomes "Our message is God's power"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek names Christ as God's power and wisdom. The CEV makes the message the subject, so Christ drops out.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ" in both phrases; the critical text (Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and others) omits it. Christ's full title is still used across the letter, e.g. 1 Corinthians 1:2-3.

records.change: Command to appoint the least esteemed becomes a rebuking question
records.note: The Greek verb can be read as an imperative or a question; the KJV takes it as a command, the CEV as a question. The same Greek is behind both.

records.change: Omits "and in your spirit, which are God's"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus or P46. The call to glorify God in the body remains.

records.change: Omits "fasting"; only prayer is mentioned
records.note: "Fasting and" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Fasting is still taught in Matthew 6:16-18 and Acts 13:2-3.

records.change: Opens "he is pulled in two directions"; wife-virgin contrast lost
records.note: The critical text joins "and he is divided" to the end of 7:33 and reads the women differently; the Textus Receptus has "there is difference between a wife and a virgin". The teaching on undivided devotion remains.

records.change: Father and his virgin daughter become an engaged couple
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "his virgin" is read by the KJV as a father's daughter, by the CEV as a man's fiancée (also in 7:37-38). It changes who decides on the marriage.

records.change: "Jesus Christ our Lord" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Jesus Christ our Lord"; the critical text reads "Jesus our Lord", omitting "Christ". Paul's having seen the risen Lord is still stated in 15:8.

records.change: "gospel of Christ" becomes "the good news"
records.note: "Of Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. The gospel is called Christ's in 9:12.

records.change: Omits "for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof"
records.note: The repeated quotation of Psalm 24:1 is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early Alexandrian witnesses. It is still quoted in 10:26.

records.change: "broken for you" becomes "given for you"; "Take" dropped
records.note: "Broken" and "Take, eat" are in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; "given" is supplied from Luke 22:19.

records.change: Omits "the Lord" in "the second man is the Lord from heaven"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus; P46, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "the second man is from heaven". Christ's heavenly origin remains; his title as Lord here does not.

records.change: "O grave" becomes death: both questions ask about death
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "O grave (hades)" in the second line; the critical text reads "O death" twice. The victory over death is unchanged.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: "Jesus Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. The curse on those who do not love the Lord remains.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus omit it. The same blessing names Christ fully elsewhere, e.g. 2 Corinthians 13:14.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The Amen is in most manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and a few others; the critical text leaves it out. The subscription that follows is not part of the letter's text.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or P46. Jesus is called Lord in 4:5.

records.change: "by Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Jesus Christ"; the critical text reads "Christ" only. Reconciliation through Christ is unchanged.

records.change: "your ready mind" becomes "we hope to help"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "your" readiness; the critical text reads "our". It shifts whose eagerness the gift shows.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The full title stands in 1:3.

records.change: "grace of Christ" becomes God's kindness; Christ not named
records.note: Most manuscripts, including the critical text, read "the grace of Christ"; P46 and a few others omit "Christ". The CEV credits the calling and kindness to God alone.

records.change: "crucified with Christ" becomes "I have died"
records.note: A translation choice; the Greek is the same. The believer's union with Christ's death is less explicit, though "Christ lives in me" remains.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" from the covenant confirmed of God
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The promise's fulfilment in Christ is stated in 3:16.

records.change: "to bring us unto Christ" becomes "until we had faith"
records.note: A translation choice; both texts read "unto Christ", which the CEV leaves out. Justification by faith is kept.

records.change: "heir of God through Christ" becomes given what he promised
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "heir of God through Christ"; the critical text reads "heir through God". Sonship through Christ is still taught in 4:4-6.

records.change: Omits "in Christ Jesus"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46 or Vaticanus. The same teaching with "in Jesus Christ" is in 5:6.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord Jesus"; the critical text reads "Jesus"; the CEV supplies "Christ". The title "Lord" is dropped here.

records.change: Omits "by Jesus Christ" from God creating all things
records.note: "By Jesus Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. Christ's role in creation is still stated in Colossians 1:16 and John 1:3.

records.change: Omits "of our Lord Jesus Christ" after "the Father"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. God is called Father of our Lord Jesus Christ in 1:3.

records.change: "fruit of the Spirit" becomes about light
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "fruit of the Spirit"; P46, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "fruit of the light". The fruit of the Spirit is still listed in Galatians 5:22.

records.change: "fear of God" becomes honouring Christ
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "of God"; the critical text reads "of Christ". Both call for reverent mutual submission.

records.change: "the Lord" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord"; the critical text reads "Christ". The same person is meant.

records.change: Omits "of his flesh, and of his bones"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. They echo Genesis 2:23, which 5:31 goes on to quote.

records.change: "Honour thy father" becomes "Obey your father"
records.note: A translation choice; the Greek (and Exodus 20:12) says "honour". Obedience is the command of 6:1, but the commandment's own word is changed.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The Amen is in most manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. The subscription that follows is not part of the letter's text.

records.change: "thought it not robbery to be equal" becomes "did not try to remain equal"
records.note: A translation choice on harpagmos; the CEV's wording can suggest Christ gave up equality with God, where the KJV says he rightly held it. Christ's deity is still stated ("Christ was truly God").

records.change: Omits "walk by the same rule, mind the same thing"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The call to be of one mind is in 2:2.

records.change: "destruction" becomes "hell"
records.note: A translation choice; the Greek word means destruction or ruin. The CEV names the place where the KJV names the end.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The Amen is in most manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and some others; the critical text leaves it out.

records.change: Omits "and the Lord Jesus Christ" from the greeting
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and other early witnesses. Christ is named as Lord throughout the letter, e.g. 1:3.

records.change: Omits "through his blood"
records.note: The phrase is in some later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or the Byzantine majority; it matches Ephesians 1:7. Peace "through the blood of his cross" is still stated in 1:20.

records.change: "firstborn from the dead" becomes "first to be raised"
records.note: A translation choice; the Greek is the same. "First to be raised" loses the sense of rank and heirship in "firstborn", though "above all others" follows.

records.change: Omits "and of the Father"; the mystery is simply Christ
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "of God, and of the Father, and of Christ"; the critical text reads "of God, Christ". The Father is still named in 1:3 and 1:12.

records.change: Drops "bodily" and "the Godhead"
records.note: A translation choice; the Greek is the same. "God lives fully in Christ" keeps his deity but loses the stress on the incarnation.

records.change: "peace of God" becomes peace from Christ
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "of God"; the critical text reads "of Christ".

records.change: "to the Lord" becomes "to God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "to the Lord"; the critical text reads "to God".

records.change: "fearing God" becomes "Honor the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the critical text reads "the Lord".

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The Amen is in most later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. The subscription that follows is not part of the letter's text.

records.change: Omits "from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and other early witnesses. The church is still said to be in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: The critical Greek text reads "our Lord Jesus"; "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus. Christ's title is kept elsewhere in the letter.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: The critical text has "our Lord Jesus" without "Christ", which the Textus Receptus adds. The title is still used in 1:1 and 5:23.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord"
records.note: The critical text lacks "Christ" (Textus Receptus has it); the CEV also drops "Jesus" as a paraphrase. The referent is still plain.

records.change: "possess his vessel" becomes "respect and honor your wife"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "vessel" may mean one's own body or one's wife; the CEV settles on wife.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not the critical text. The subscription is a later scribal note, not part of the verse.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: The critical text reads "our Lord Jesus"; "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus.

records.change: First "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: The critical text lacks "Christ" in the first phrase; the Textus Receptus has it. The full title remains at the end of the verse.

records.change: "day of Christ" becomes "the Lord has already come"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "day of Christ"; the critical text and most early manuscripts read "day of the Lord".

records.change: Omits "as God" before sitting in the temple
records.note: "As God" is in the Textus Receptus but absent from the critical text; the claim to be God is still stated.

records.change: "from the beginning" becomes "the first ones to be saved"
records.note: Manuscripts divide between "from the beginning" (ap' arches, Textus Receptus) and "firstfruits" (aparchen); the CEV follows the latter, turning an eternal choice into a first in time.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus, not the critical text. The subscription is a scribal note.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text reads "Christ Jesus". Jesus is called Lord in 1:2.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" from "I speak the truth"
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the critical text. Paul's truthfulness is still affirmed.

records.change: "God was manifest" becomes "Christ came"
records.note: Sinaiticus and other early witnesses read "who" (hos), the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus "God" (theos); the CEV supplies "Christ", so the verse no longer calls him God.

records.change: Omits "in spirit" from the list of examples
records.note: "In spirit" is in the Textus Receptus and Byzantine text but not in the early manuscripts the critical text follows.

records.change: "having damnation" becomes "become guilty"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek krima means judgment or condemnation; the CEV softens it to guilt.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text reads "Christ Jesus".

records.change: Omits "from such withdraw thyself"
records.note: The command is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or D; the same instruction is in 2 Timothy 3:5.

records.change: Omits "Amen"; "with thee" becomes "all of you"
records.note: The critical text reads "with you" (plural) and has no "Amen"; the Textus Receptus has "with thee" and "Amen". The subscription is a scribal note.

records.change: Adds that the Lord Jesus asks God for mercy
records.note: A translation choice: the KJV's "the Lord grant... mercy of the Lord" is read as Jesus interceding with God, which the text does not state.

records.change: "before the Lord" becomes "with God as your witness"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord"; many early manuscripts and the critical text read "God".

records.change: "name of Christ" becomes "worships the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; the critical text reads "the Lord" (kyriou).

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text reads "Christ Jesus". His role as judge is kept.

records.change: "The Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord"; omits "Amen"
records.note: The critical text reads only "the Lord" and lacks "Amen"; the Textus Receptus has "Lord Jesus Christ" and "Amen". The subscription is a scribal note.

records.change: Omits "mercy"; "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The critical text reads "grace and peace" and "Christ Jesus our Saviour"; the Textus Receptus adds "mercy" and "Lord".

records.change: Omits "Amen"; "grace" becomes "the Lord will be kind"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not the critical text. The subscription is a scribal note.

records.change: "in you" becomes "given us"; "Christ Jesus" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The critical text reads "in us" and "in Christ"; the Textus Receptus reads "in you" and "in Christ Jesus".

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not the critical text. The subscription is a scribal note.

records.change: Omits "by himself" before purging sins
records.note: "By himself" is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; it stresses Christ alone made the cleansing, which Hebrews 9:12-14 still states.

records.change: "I have begotten thee" becomes "I have become your Father"
records.note: A translation choice for gegenneka; the CEV drops "begotten", though the Father-Son relation is kept.

records.change: "God... hath anointed thee" becomes "I, your God, have chosen you"
records.note: A translation choice: "anointed" (the Messiah's anointing) becomes "chosen", and the address to the Son is recast as God speaking.

records.change: "the son of man" becomes "weaklings such as we"
records.note: A translation choice: Hebrews applies Psalm 8's "son of man" to Jesus (2:9); the CEV makes it generic humanity, weakening the link.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ Jesus"; the critical text reads only "Jesus".

records.change: "have I begotten thee" becomes "I have become your Father"
records.note: A translation choice for gegenneka; "begotten" is dropped, though Christ is still called God's Son.

records.change: "through the eternal Spirit" becomes "an eternal and spiritual sacrifice"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek names the eternal Spirit as the one through whom Christ offered himself; the CEV makes it describe the sacrifice.

records.change: Omits "saith the Lord" after "I will recompense"
records.note: "Saith the Lord" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the critical text. The quotation is still attributed to God.

records.change: Omits "in heaven"
records.note: "In heaven" is in the Textus Receptus but absent from the early manuscripts the critical text follows.

records.change: "only begotten son" becomes "only son"
records.note: A translation choice for monogenes; here it describes Isaac, the unique son of promise.

records.change: "church of the firstborn" becomes "God's dearest children"
records.note: A translation choice: the CEV drops "firstborn" and "assembly", losing the picture of the firstborn's inheritance.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not the critical text. The subscription is a scribal note.

records.change: "which the Lord hath promised" becomes "he rewards"
records.note: The Textus Receptus names "the Lord"; the critical text reads only "he promised". "Crown of life" is also paraphrased.

records.change: Omits God having "chosen" the poor
records.note: A translation choice: the CEV makes God give the poor faith, dropping his choosing of them.

records.change: "justified by works" becomes "pleased God by"
records.note: A translation choice: James's word "justified" is dropped, which blurs his argument with Paul's use of the term.

records.change: "God, even the Father" becomes "our Lord and Father"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God and Father"; the critical text reads "the Lord and Father".

records.change: Omits "through the Spirit"
records.note: "Through the Spirit" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the critical text. The Spirit's sanctifying is stated in 1:2.

records.change: Adds "and be saved"
records.note: "Unto salvation" is in P72, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus but not in the Byzantine majority or Textus Receptus; it can read as salvation reached by growth.

records.change: "the Lord God" becomes "Christ... the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord God"; the critical text reads "Christ as Lord".

records.change: Omits "for us" after "Christ hath suffered"
records.note: "For us" is in the Byzantine majority and Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus or some other early witnesses; Christ's substitutionary suffering is still stated in 1 Peter 2:21 and 3:18.

records.change: Omits "on their part he is evil spoken of...glorified"
records.note: The final clause is in the Textus Receptus and Byzantine text but not in the early manuscripts the critical text follows.

records.change: Omits "Amen"; "Christ Jesus" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The critical text reads "in Christ" and lacks "Amen"; the Textus Receptus has "Christ Jesus" and "Amen".

records.change: "denying the Lord" becomes "don't really belong to the Master"
records.note: A translation choice: denial of the Master becomes not belonging to him, changing what the verse says of those bought.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from the reserved darkness
records.note: "For ever" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the critical text; the CEV's "darkest part of hell" keeps the judgment.

records.change: "Jesus Christ his Son" becomes "his Son Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Jesus Christ"; the critical text reads only "Jesus".

records.change: "only begotten Son" becomes "only Son"
records.note: A translation choice for monogenes; many modern versions render it "only" or "one and only". Christ's unique sonship is kept.

records.change: Omits "in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost"
records.note: The Johannine Comma is in the Textus Receptus and some late Greek and Latin manuscripts, but not in the Greek manuscripts before the late Middle Ages. The Trinity is taught elsewhere, as in Matthew 28:19.

records.change: Omits "in earth"
records.note: "In earth" belongs to the Johannine Comma, absent from the critical text along with 5:7's heavenly witnesses.

records.change: Omits final "that ye may believe on the name" clause
records.note: The closing clause is in the Textus Receptus but not in the critical text. Faith in the Son of God is still stated.

records.change: "keepeth himself" becomes "God's own Son protects them"
records.note: Manuscripts divide between "himself" (Textus Receptus) and "him"; the CEV follows the latter and reads the begotten one as Christ.

records.change: "This is the true God" applied to the Father, not Jesus
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "This is the true God" may refer to Jesus Christ just named; the CEV makes it the Father.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not the critical text.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord Jesus Christ"; the critical text reads "Jesus Christ".

records.change: "transgresseth" becomes "keep changing"; second "of Christ" omitted
records.note: The critical text reads "goes ahead" (proagon) for "transgresseth" and lacks the second "of Christ"; the Textus Receptus has both.

records.change: Omits closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not the critical text.

records.change: "the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes one title
records.note: The critical text lacks "God", making "only Master and Lord" both titles of Jesus Christ; the Textus Receptus names God and Christ.

records.change: "first begotten of the dead" paraphrased; "washed" becomes "set free"
records.note: "First begotten" is paraphrased; "washed" (lousanti, Textus Receptus) and "freed" (lysanti, critical text) are a textual variant. Cleansing by blood is kept.

records.change: Omits "the beginning and the ending"; "Lord" becomes "Lord God"
records.note: Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and most Greek manuscripts lack the title and read "Lord God"; the Textus Receptus follows a few late witnesses. The same title stands in Revelation 21:6 and 22:13.

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus" twice
records.note: The critical text reads "in Jesus" and "of Jesus"; the Textus Receptus adds "Christ" both times.

records.change: Omits "I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in the early manuscripts the critical text follows. Christ is still called "the first and the last" in 1:17.

records.change: Omits "Amen"; "hell" becomes "world of the dead"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus, not the critical text; "hell" translates Hades, which the CEV renders as the world of the dead.

records.change: Omits "quickly"
records.note: "Quickly" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the critical text.

records.change: Omits "which thing I hate"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "which thing I hate"; the critical text reads "likewise". Christ's hatred of their deeds is stated in 2:6.

records.change: Omits "him that liveth for ever and ever"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus but not in the critical text; the elders still worship.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "Death's Kingdom"
records.note: A translation choice: "hell" translates Hades, the realm of the dead, which the CEV renders as Death's Kingdom.

records.change: "an angel flying" becomes "a lone eagle flying"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads 'angel' (angelou); Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority read 'eagle' (aetou), which the CEV follows. The warning itself is unchanged.

records.change: "the God of the earth" becomes "the Lord who rules the earth"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads 'God' (theou); most manuscripts read 'Lord' (kyriou), which the CEV follows. Both refer to God.

records.change: "his Christ" becomes "his Chosen One"; "kingdoms" made singular
records.note: 'Chosen One' is the CEV's rendering of Christos (Anointed) here; the singular 'kingdom' follows the critical text against the Textus Receptus plural. The title 'Christ' is not used.

records.change: Omits "and art to come"
records.note: The phrase is lacking in nearly all Greek manuscripts, including the Byzantine majority; the Textus Receptus has it from a few late witnesses. Without it the hymn presents God's coming as now fulfilled in his reign; the threefold title stands in 1:4, 1:8 and 4:8.

records.change: "the power of his Christ" becomes "God's own Chosen One"
records.note: A translation choice: the CEV renders Christos as 'Chosen One' rather than 'Christ'. The Greek is the same in all texts.

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus adds 'Christ' (Christou); the major manuscripts read only 'Jesus', which the CEV follows.

records.change: "from the foundation of the world" moved from "slain" to names written
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek allows the phrase to go with 'the Lamb slain' (KJV) or with names 'written' (CEV, compare 17:8). The KJV's reading of a Lamb slain before creation is lost here.

records.change: Omits "before the throne of God"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or most manuscripts; the CEV follows the latter.

records.change: "King of saints" becomes "ruler of all nations"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads 'saints' (hagion), with weak support; most manuscripts read 'nations' (ethnon), others 'ages'. The CEV follows 'nations'.

records.change: Omits "O Lord"; "shalt be" becomes "the holy God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has 'O Lord' and 'which shalt be' (ho esomenos); the manuscripts omit 'Lord' and read 'the Holy One' (ho hosios), which the CEV follows.

records.change: Omits "of heaven" after "the temple"
records.note: 'Of heaven' is in the Textus Receptus and the Byzantine majority but not in Alexandrinus and other early witnesses, which the CEV follows.

records.change: "unto the Lord our God" becomes "to our God"
records.note: 'Lord' (kyrio) is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or most manuscripts; the CEV follows the latter.

records.change: "stand before God" becomes "standing in front of that throne"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads 'before God'; the manuscripts read 'before the throne', which the CEV follows. The throne is God's (20:11), so the sense is kept.

records.change: "death and hell" becomes "death and its kingdom"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek is Hades, the realm of the dead, which the KJV renders 'hell'. The final judgment is still stated.

records.change: "death and hell" becomes "death and its kingdom"
records.note: A translation choice for Hades, as in 20:13. The lake of fire as the second death is kept.

records.change: "out of heaven" becomes "from the throne"; omits "be their God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads 'out of heaven'; Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read 'from the throne', which the CEV follows. 'And be their God' is uncertain in the manuscripts and left out.

records.change: "God shall wipe away" becomes "He will wipe"
records.note: 'God' (ho theos) is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus; the CEV follows the latter. The referent is still God from 21:3.

records.change: "he shall be my son" becomes "they will be my people"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek says 'son' (huios) in all texts. The promise of sonship becomes a promise of belonging to God's people.

records.change: Omits "of them which are saved"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or the majority of manuscripts; the CEV follows the latter.

records.change: "do his commandments" becomes "have washed their robes"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and Byzantine majority read 'do his commandments'; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read 'wash their robes', which the CEV follows. The ground of the right to the tree of life changes from obedience to cleansing (compare 7:14).

records.change: "the book of life" becomes "the life-giving tree"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads 'book of life' with almost no Greek support; the manuscripts read 'tree of life', which the CEV follows. The warning of losing a share in the holy city is kept.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"; omits "Amen"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has 'our', 'Christ' and 'Amen'; Alexandrinus reads 'the Lord Jesus' without them, which the CEV follows.
